picks.headline: Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech Football vs. SMU
picks.blurb: DALLAS — Virginia Tech football has a towering tilt on its hands today: SMU — the best opponent the Hokies have played all year. Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) became bowl-eligible after capturing a 20-16 victory over Clemson — its first over the Tigers since 2007 — and did not play this past week. SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) won six of its first seven games before a 30-27 stumble against Syracuse in the JMA Wireless Dome in Upstate New York. Both teams remain in contention for a spot in the ACC Championship Game and in the top-five unranked squads receiving votes for the AP Top 25, making Friday's contest particularly consequential as the regular season enters its final month. The Mustangs have been nearly untouchable at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, winning all five of their home games this season and each of their 11 ACC home contests since joining the conference in 2024. Virginia Tech, meanwhile, has already captured three road victories against Power Four opponents this season, including breaking its nearly-20-year drought against the Tigers. The Hokies and Mustangs haven't met since 1974, when SMU secured a 28-25 victory. More than five decades later, their first meeting as ACC opponents features two prolific quarterbacks and a pair of potent yet at-times inconsistent defenses. Here's a look at both teams ahead of Friday night's showdown. Virginia Tech's Offense Virginia Tech's offense has found its footing under quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer, who has completed 71.4% of his passes for 2,140 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just two interceptions through eight games. The Penn State transfer has provided a steady presence at center, throwing for at least 250 yards in five contests. However, the Hokies' offensive line has struggled to protect him at times, surrendering six sacks against Clemson. Grunkemeyer's top target has been wide receiver Que'Sean Brown, who leads the team with 685 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 51 receptions. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also emerged as a reliable option, collecting 50 receptions for 493 yards and a team-high six receiving scores. Reynolds caught the game-winning touchdown against Clemson, hauling in a fourth-and-1 pass with 1:44 remaining to put Virginia Tech ahead. On the ground, Jeffrey Overton Jr. has paced the Hokies with 639 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 113 carries, averaging 5.7 yards per carry. Marcellous Hawkins has added 337 yards and five rushing touchdowns, giving Virginia Tech another option out of the backfield. SMU's Offense SMU's offense has been one of the ACC's most productive units this season, averaging 35.3 points and 460-plus yards per game. Quarterback Kevin Jennings has been at the epicenter of that success, completing 73.7% of his passes for 2,414 yards, 21 touchdowns and five interceptions. The fifth-year signal-caller ranks among the nation's leaders in passing efficiency and surpassed 10,000 career passing yards in last week's loss to Syracuse. Jennings threw for 351 yards and two touchdowns against the Orange, but the Mustangs couldn't hold onto their late lead, conceding a game-winning Syracuse touchdown with 17 seconds remaining. Wide receiver Yamir Knight has been one of Jennings' primary targets, leading SMU with 523 receiving yards on 44 receptions and three touchdowns. Knight caught six passes for 80 yards and a touchdown against Syracuse. Running back Kendrick Raphael has provided balance to the Mustangs' passing attack, rushing for 692 yards and nine touchdowns on 135 carries. Raphael is no stranger to Virginia Tech, having scored three touchdowns against the Hokies last season while playing for California. His third touchdown tied the score late in regulation before Virginia Tech prevailed 42-34 in double overtime. Virginia Tech's Defense If Virginia Tech is going to leave Dallas with its seventh victory, its defense must make Jennings uncomfortable. The Hokies lead the nation with 77 tackles for loss and rank sixth nationally in sacks, having brought opposing quarterbacks down 27 times through eight games. Defensive end Aycen Stevens has spearheaded that effort with eight sacks, while defensive tackle Kemari Copeland has contributed four tackles for loss. Virginia Tech's defensive front was particularly disruptive against Clemson, accumulating 13 tackles for loss and four sacks while holding the Tigers to 16 points. In the secondary, cornerback Jaquez White delivered one of the game's defining plays, sacking Clemson's quarterback on the Tigers' final possession on a corner blitz. White finished with a team-high 11 tackles, helping Virginia Tech preserve its four-point advantage. Linebacker Keon Wylie has also been a consistent contributor, recording 41 tackles this season. The Hokies have been especially effective against the run, allowing just 93.4 rushing yards per game. However, their secondary has been less imposing, recording only two interceptions. Against a quarterback of Jennings' caliber, Virginia Tech's ability to generate pressure without exposing its secondary could prove decisive. SMU's Defense SMU's defense presents another difficult challenge for a Virginia Tech offense that has occasionally struggled with pass protection. The Mustangs have registered 22 sacks this season, led by defensive lineman Marques White's 5.5. Linebacker Alexander Kilgore paces the team with 41 tackles. SMU has been particularly effective on third down, allowing opponents to convert just 31 of 115 attempts — a 27% success rate that ranks No. 3 in the nation. The Mustangs have also been difficult to attack through the air, surrendering just 181.8 passing yards per game. Virginia Tech's ability to establish its running game with Overton and Hawkins could be particularly important, especially considering the Hokies were held to just 70 rushing yards against Clemson. Final Thoughts Friday's contest could come down to which team controls the line of scrimmage. Virginia Tech has made a habit of disrupting opposing backfields, but SMU possesses one of the most efficient quarterbacks in college football. Conversely, the Mustangs' pass rush will test an offensive line that has struggled to keep Grunkemeyer upright. The Hokies have already demonstrated their ability to win away from Blacksburg, but Gerald J. Ford Stadium presents a different challenge. SMU has yet to lose at home this season, and the Mustangs will be eager to respond after their disappointing trip to Syracuse. I think SMU will win but that it'll be far from easy. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-6) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 2-1 Last meeting: SMU 28, Virginia Tech 25 — September 21, 1974 Current streak: SMU, 2 (1973-74) Setting the scene While No. 1 Miami (FL) and No. 14 Wake Forest are the only ACC teams that reside in the AP Top 25, the conference title race is far from finished. There are five two-loss teams lurking right behind, and two of them clash Friday night in Dallas. It's the first meeting between SMU and Virginia Tech as ACC opponents, however, it's a familiar head coaching matchup: Rhett Lashlee and James Franklin stood on opposite sidelines as recently as 2024 in the College Football Playoff. There's plenty on the line for the bowl eligible opponents. A win would do wonders for remaining in the ACC race, especially for SMU, which can still capture a tiebreaker against Wake Forest. But a third conference loss is essentially an elimination in a 17-team league. Virginia Tech Hokies outlook BLACKSBURG, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 17: Head coach James Franklin of the Virginia Tech Hokies greets Kaleb Spencer #3 before the game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets at Lane Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Blacksburg, Virginia. (Photo by Michael Shroyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) can make another statement on the road after its bye week. The Hokies haven't rattled off seven wins in a regular season since 2019, but that streak could end Friday in year one of the James Franklin era. Virginia Tech is fresh off its biggest win under Franklin, taking down Clemson 20-16 in Death Valley on Oct. 24. Close games have been commonplace for the Hokies this season. Each of their last six contests were decided by 10 points or fewer. Three featured lead changes in the final five minutes, while another ended on a missed field goal attempt that would have resulted in a lead change. The restoration of Virginia Tech football can be attributed to the passing game. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer followed Franklin from Penn State and has drastically improved in his junior campaign. Grunkemeyer has connected on an efficient 71.4 percent of attempts — seventh nationally among quarterbacks with 100 attempts — and has delivered 17 touchdowns against two interceptions. Grunkemeyer has eclipsed 300 yards three times and finished seven of his eight starts without throwing a pick. Two receivers have carried a bulk of the load. Wide receiver Que'Sean Brown ranks atop the team with 51 receptions and 685 receiving yards, and he's secured at least five receptions in all eight games. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also been a matchup nightmare for defenses. Reynolds' 50 receptions rank first and his 491 receiving yards ranks third among all FBS tight ends. While a bulk of his production occurred in September, his outing against Clemson was a productive one, snagging two touchdowns on seven receptions. The Hokies aren't as adept in the run game, where they check in at 111th in the FBS with 3.7 yards per carry. They don't incorporate much quarterbaack mobility and primarily rely on the duo of Jeffrey Overton Jr. and Marcellous Hawkins Jr. Overton, a common weapon in the receiving game, showed the extent of his powers in a 209-yard rushing explosion against Boston College. Hawkins has been a steady secondary back, and he's tied for the team lead with five rushing touchdowns. Virginia Tech only surrendered more than 26 points once this season, and that was a Friday night matchup against Pittsburgh. The Hokies' defense has been a positive for the team, tied for 35th in points allowed and ranked 27th in yards allowed per game. Their strength involves limiting the run, where they give up just 93.4 yards per game on a 3.0 average. Sacks heavily factor into that total, and Virginia Tech is the best in the ACC and the sixth-best in the nation at getting to the quarterback, producing 3.4 sacks per game. It's a defensive end led effort. Aycen Stevens ranks first in the conference with 8.0 sacks, while his fellow defensive ends Cortez Harris and Mylachi Williams have 5.0 and 4.5, respectively. The Hokies haven't been as strong on the back end, but they prevent explosive plays well. No team has recorded a 50-yard completion on this defense all season. But what Virginia Tech needs to improve upon is its turnover output. The Hokies forced just five takeaways through eight games, causing the team to enter Friday with a minus-4 in the turnover battle this season. SMU Mustangs outlook DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 17: Southern Methodist University Mustangs defensive end Marques White (16) rushes the passer during the game between SMU and Virginia on October 17, 2026 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by George Walker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) dropped from the rankings after a heartbreaking 30-27 loss at Syracuse last weekend. It was only the Mustangs' fourth conference defeat since joining the ACC, and the third in which they held a lead in the final minute. However, SMU has never lost back-to-back ACC games and owns an 11-0 record in ACC play at home, giving Rhett Lashlee's team the perfect opportunity to bounce back and remain in the conference title race. Slow starts have been the Mustangs' kryptonite. In their last five ACC games, they haven't scored more than 13 points in a half or entered the break with a lead larger than three. However, they've won each of their last five second halves, finishing a plus-68 over that span. SMU's offense is led by Kevin Jennings, who is one of seven passers averaging over 300 yards per game. This season has been a masterclass in efficiency for the senior, who is completing passes at a 73.7 percent clip — the third-highest rate in the country among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. Jennings has also thrown 152 consecutive passes without an interception, with his last misfire coming in the first quarter of a Sept. 26 matchup against Missouri State. The Mustangs' receiver room is as deep as they come, with five different players over the 200-yard threshold. Yamir Knight is the leader with 44 receptions for 523 yards, while Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale can also pose as explosive threats for an offense that ranks fifth nationally in 50+ yard receptions. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrstrom are also incorporated into the passing game, and they tie for the team lead with four receptions apiece. Unlike SMU's first ACC defeat at Louisville, last Saturday's loss to Syracuse was largely determined in the trenches. The Mustangs uncharacteristically allowed six sacks, accounting for 43 percent of their season total. Additionally, they struggled to create space for the running backs, which never broke off an explosive gain. Kendrick Raphael has posted three 100-yard games already in ACC play, and he can also do damage out of the backfield as a receiving option. SMU's defense didn't necessarily have a bad outing at Syracuse, limiting the Orange to 5.9 yards per passing attempt and 3.7 yards per rush. But the Mustangs surrendered conversions on all four of Syracuse's fourth down attempts, allowing the Orange to sustain otherwise lost drives. A veteran defensive line full of super seniors is the strength of the unit. SMU ranks 15th nationally with 2.9 sacks per game, and eighth-year senior Marques White leads the way with 5.5 sacks, while the rest of the sacks are quite evenly distributed. The pressure goes hand-in-hand with a strong passing defense, and SMU ranks 28th nationally in fewest passing yards allowed at 182 per game. That is the most improved element of the Mustangs from last year, but losing starting strong safety Tyren Polley for the year could make things difficult down the road. Sael Reyes stepped up last game with 10 tackles in his second start of the season, while Jimmy Wyrick recorded eight from the other safety spot. Lastly, turnovers have been a significant determinant in SMU results this season. The Mustangs lost the turnover battle 5-0 in their two losses, and they're the only bowl eligible team at a minus-5 or worse this season. These 6-2 teams are structured somewhat similarly: strong passing attacks with tight end utilization, dominant defensive fronts that repeatedly get to the quarterback, and solid defenses hampered by poor turnover margins. Short weeks oftentimes favor the home team, and SMU remains perfect against ACC opponents at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Given SMU's discrepancy between first and second half performance, Virginia Tech may enter halftime with the lead, but the Mustangs ultimately rally behind Kevin Jennings in the fourth quarter to secure a one-score win on The Hilltop. Prediction: SMU 30, Virginia Tech 24

Ahead of the clash, here's our staff's predictions as to what will unfold tonight in the Lone Star State. JACKSON CAUDELL: While it will still be a long shot even if they find a way to win, the Hokies' ACC hopes are on the line tomorrow night at SMU. The Mustangs are also battling for their ACC title hopes, and that makes this a fascinating matchup. This is a chance for James Franklin to land another win against one of the better programs in the conference, and I think they have the offense to take advantage of a suspect SMU defense. If the Hokies can get after Kevin Jennings and force a few turnovers, I think they are able to do that and score a big win. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 31, SMU 27 JAMES DUNCAN: Syracuse left a blueprint last Saturday, beating SMU 30-27 on a touchdown with 17 seconds left. Virginia Tech is built to follow it. Nobody has beaten the Hokies by more than five points this season, and they come in with 13 days of rest to SMU's six. Ethan Grunkemeyer has thrown 17 touchdowns and two interceptions, and both picks came in one night against Pitt. He won't hand Kevin Jennings free possessions, which puts the game on Brent Pry's defense. That group made 13 tackles for loss at Clemson, and it won't need half that many Friday if it gets off the field on third down. Friday won't be a rout, but I think the Hokies give the Mustangs their first home loss in the ACC. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 30, SMU 28 THOMAS HUGHES: Let's get this out of the way: SMU has never lost an ACC game at home. Its strongest wins at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season, however, came against Virginia and California - two squads with a combined 7-11 (4-8 ACC) record. The Hokies should be well-equipped to contend with the Mustangs, though SMU signal-caller Kevin Jennings may present Tech with its toughest test of the season yet. Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer has been stellar this campaign, throwing 17 touchdowns to just two interceptions, and while I expect another strong performance from him, I think SMU narrowly edges Virginia Tech in Dallas tonight. Final score prediction: SMU 31, Virginia Tech 28 KADEN REINHARD: I think this game will be defined by one word over the 60 minutes of action: Intensity. Several factors will fuel that fire: Friday night lights, the Mustangs coming off the Syracuse loss and Tech finding itself back in the receiving-votes category of the AP Top 25. But most importantly, I see both offenses locking into a close-knit battle, as both sides can mend their attacks with a healthy mix of the ground and air attack. Ultimately, I think the Hokies' defense can handle the contest by not allowing SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings to extend many plays outside the pocket, which has been a struggle for the Hokies in recent years. picks.blurb: Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions Stike up the Hokie Pokey, Tech Triumph, and the Victory Tag. | John Schneider - SB Nation John Schneider · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:59 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a short week after a week break. The Hokies are heading to Dallas to face off against the Southern Methodist University Mustangs. The Hokies are up against another major ACC opponent, and winning the game means advancing in the ACC and potentially seeing a ranking. Crossover Week Mayhem Just a note from us: Well, the first week in November through the first week of December is always a challenge for coverage. The soccer teams are wrapping up with decent enough records, but their seasons aren't quite over. The Women's Basketball Team has opened their home record at 2-0, and the Men's team also graced Cassell with a W. All of that puts a real strain on coverage so bear with us as we sort out schedules, and fight fall health issues and work vs. Hokie sports balance. The football team isn't finished, though. There are still four games left on the schedule, and then we get to plan on bowl coverage this season. Isn't that a happy event? The Hokies are bowl eligible just a couple of games after the halfway point, and that's a very pleasant occurrence. To think that we are actually paying attention to the bowl invitation list, instead of worrying on Thanksgiving weekend whether or not a win will net an invitation somewhere. The first thing to cover is a bit of fun. The ACC Network desk hosts Eric McClain and Eddie Royal had a bet going. Remember, McClain is a former Clemson player, and we all know and love Eddie Royal. So, the bet was that the loser had to wear the winner's mascot costume. Eddie was not dressed as a Tiger with the googly eyes for the TV segment. ( Congratulations to the Virginia Tech Cheer Squad equipment folks and Travis Wells for getting most of an actual Hokie Bird big enough for Eric. ) The Virginia Tech Wrestling Team received a massive boost from a wrestler who hasn't even wrestled his first match as a Hokie, yet, but who is already a world champion. Freshman Bo Bassett traveled to Kazakhstan and netted the program its first world championship and was the first American in 20 years to win in his weight class (65KG – for those lacking metric conversion skills that's 143 pounds ). The Coach Robie is going to have an absolutely dominant wrestling team this season. Back to Football Stuff It looks like the team is going to be wearing head to toe all-whites for this one. Go get your coffee, or a quick snack and listen in on Coach Franklin's weekly presser. As Bryan posted up earlier, this time the Hokies have some really good news coming out of the locker room as it pertains to the Offensive Line. Montavious Cunningham and Brody Meadows are back up to speed and are expected to play on Friday night. The O-Line has been dipping into the #3s on the depth chart for the past few games, and getting them back is a serious update to the struggling run game. That All Leads to This… Predictions The SMU Mustangs are largely a Big XII import with a near automatic bubble to the top of the ACC football pile. It's Dallas, TX, and football is a near religion for Texas. That means the program is well funded, with premium coaching, and players doused liberally with NIL funding. Up until last weekend, the Mustangs were sporting a very respectable one loss record. Until they showed up in the Syracuse (whatever they call the Carrier Dome, now), as expected in the beginning of the season SMU was challenging hard for the #2 bid in the ACC fake Championship game ( until the conference goes back to divisions and division champs who play everyone else in the division the game in Charlotte will remain fake to me ). Then the Mustangs got treated to the old Big East upset win by the Orange. That knocked them down a peg but also put the Hokies in the position of earning the #3 spot on the ACC leader board. That all means that this game might not mean an ACC bid, but it will mean a much better bowl game situation over the holidays. Bowls mean big broadcast money, and the program needs the cash to make up for a restricted gate at Lane. The Mustangs are favored by slightly less than a touchdown for this one, in their house no less. We'll see how we feel about that. This is a big test for the Hokies. Virginia Tech had a huge win at Clemson two weeks ago. No, this isn't the same Clemson team as only a few years ago, but it means something for other ACC teams to walk into Death Valley and win. SMU is better than the Tigers, but they aren't unbeatable. The clear difference here is the quarterback position. SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings is a stud. He also has one of the ACC's best running backs and one of the top receiving units in the league. This is a huge challenge for VT defensive coordinator Brent Pry. Offensively, I think the Hokies have success moving the ball. SMU's size on the defensive interior concerns me, especially with Tech's OL struggles. There is hope that with Cunningham and Meadows back, the offensive line is better, but we'll see. I expect a close game. My heart says the Hokies, my head says SMU in a close one. SMU 34, Hokies 31 This game all depends on how the Mustangs adjusted to their Syracuse loss, and if the Hokies on both sides of the ball can adjust to how the Orange controlled the SMU offense, and how they managed to get by their defense. SMU, interestingly enough, has a similar offensive/defensive balance to Tech's than we have seen this season. There are lots of "IFs" in this game, and the biggest one is "IF" the Tech defense can limit the SMU offense to what it's been scoring over the season against peer teams, the Hokies have a much better chance to win than the listed 6-point betting gimme to SMU. The latest projected O/U is 56.5, which tells me volumes of information. The analysts see this as a very close game, and the end result being less than a full score between the two teams. If the Hokies stay away from getting enamored of the run game and go downfield fast and consistently in the air on quick developing intermediate routes to their best receivers, there will be run opportunities. If Tech decides to try to "establish the run" the offense could bog down into chronic 3-and-outs. The return of two key #1/#2 depth chart players is not an excuse to try to revert to 1960's caveman Johnny Unitas two runs and a pass offense. If the Hokies move the ball and do it fast, they have enough defense ( which needs to put serious pressure on the quarterback on every play ) to hold the Mustangs to a 3.5 score effort. The Hokies are capable of 4 or more. That's a whole lot of "Ifs" though. Here's the skinny… the first team to score over 30 points wins. That puts my prediction hat on, and I think the Hokies might just be good for it, regardless of the conditions. Just a quick reminder of the times and broadcast information. It's an ESPN deal.

Win out, though, and it has a great shot when it comes down to the tiebreakers. Virginia Tech has won two in a row, and it gets Miami in a few weeks. Virginia Tech is No. 1 in the nation in tackles for loss, coming up with 13 in the win over Clemson two weeks ago, along with four sacks. SMU is okay in pass protection, and it's solid at times with the running game, but there's a problem when it turns the ball over – the two giveaways against Syracuse were a big deal. The three turnovers in the loss to Louisville mattered. However … Why SMU Will Win Virginia Tech doesn't take the ball away enough. The two takeaways helped stop Georgia Tech in a 34-24 win, but the Hokies have only forced six turnovers, and none in five games. SMU has to get its tempo going. Counteract the Virginia Tech pass rush with quick-hitting throws, keep the defense on its heels, and, on the other side, get the defense off the field. Virginia Tech isn't always great on third downs, and SMU is third in the nation, with offenses converting just 27% of their chances. SMU hasn't allowed more than 125 this year at home. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. SMU
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. SMU - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Three Bold Predictions for Virginia Tech vs. SMU Virginia Tech Hokies tight end Luke Reynolds (85) scores near Clemson safety Jerome Carter III (6) during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium Saturday, October 24, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect James Duncan · Virginia Tech Hokies On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 2:37 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Seventeen seconds remained in the JMA Wireless Dome on Saturday, when Syracuse quarterback Steve Angeli found tight end Noah Meyers alone on the left side of the end zone. Meyers had never scored for the Orange before that catch. The touchdown beat SMU 30-27 and knocked the Mustangs out of the AP Top 25. Virginia Tech should have that clip on a loop. The Hokies (6-2, 3-2 ACC) visit SMU (6-2, 4-2) at 7 p.m. ET Friday on ESPN. The Mustangs are 5-0 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season and 6.5-point favorites. Their defense holds up better against the pass than the run, and its injuries are stacked in the middle of the field. Two of my predictions start there. The third starts with what Syracuse did to Kevin Jennings. 1. Luke Reynolds has his best game since September SMU doesn't give much away through the air. Opponents complete 62.6% of their passes and average 6.0 yards per attempt. The one real hole is at safety. Sophomore Tyren Polley Jr., third on the team with 34 tackles, tore a pectoral muscle in October and is out for the season. SMU has played two games without him: a 59-20 win over Cal and the loss at Syracuse. Help could be coming. Ahmaad Moses, a first-team All-ACC safety in 2025, is questionable after missing the whole season while SMU works on his eligibility. The junior tight end has 50 catches for 493 yards and six touchdowns, and his 50 catches lead all FBS tight ends. The last three games have been quieter: 13 catches for 120 yards since Pitt. Two of those 13 went for touchdowns at Clemson, including the go-ahead score in the fourth quarter. Friday, he clears 100 receiving yards for the third time this season and finds the end zone again. 2. Jeffrey Overton Jr. snaps his 100-yard drought Overton last reached 100 yards on Sept. 26, when he ran for 209 at Boston College, the sixth-highest single-game total in Virginia Tech history. He has 230 yards in four games since and averaged 2.6 yards per carry at Clemson. The sophomore still leads the Hokies with 639 yards on 113 carries. Two things change Friday. The first is the offensive line. "We're going to get some guys back, which is helpful, especially on the offensive line," coach James Franklin said Monday. Guard/tackle Montavious Cunningham and guard Brody Meadows are expected to play. Left tackle Justin Terry is still out. The second is the defense across from him. SMU allows 125.9 rushing yards per game and 3.8 yards per carry. Those numbers flatter the Mustangs. College football counts sacks as rushing plays, and SMU has 23 sacks for 148 yards. Pull them out, and opponents are averaging 4.8 yards per designed run. Those 23 sacks matter for Virginia Tech in another way. Ethan Grunkemeyer has been sacked 23 times himself. A run game that works keeps the Hokies on schedule and gives SMU's rushers something else to think about. Overton gets his third 100-yard game of the season. 3. Virginia Tech sacks Kevin Jennings at least four times Before Halloween, SMU hadn't allowed more than two sacks in a game this season. Syracuse got six. Look at who was playing on the left side. True freshman Drew Evers moved over from right tackle to start at left tackle, and fellow true freshman Sam Utu made his first career start beside him at left guard. It was only the second college game of his career. SMU could get some help back. Guard Alex Woods, a starter, missed Syracuse, and tackle Andrew Chamblee, who has started at both tackle spots, hasn't played since Oct. 17. Neither is on Thursday's availability report. Watch the first series to see who lines up on the left. Either way, Virginia Tech has the rushers to test it. The Hokies average 3.4 sacks per game, sixth in FBS, and three players have more than four: Aycen Stevens with eight, Cortez Harris with five and Mylachi Williams with 4.5. Defensive tackle Kemari Copeland said this week the plan is to "cage" Jennings and take away his scrambles to the right. Friday, the Hokies get to Jennings at least four times. picks.blurb: How Bear Bachmeier's four INTs doomed Cougars in Holy War loss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates How Bear Bachmeier's four INTs doomed Cougars in Holy War loss Craig Meyer, USA TODAY NETWORK · USA TODAY Sports Sat, November 7, 2026 at 4:03 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The rivalry between Utah and BYU isn't just a football game. It's a war — a Holy War, to be exact. This year, the ramifications of that Biblical clash were larger than they've ever been, at least in recent memory. And it was the Utes who were able to come away with a victory. Watch BYU vs. Utah football live with Fubo (free trial) In one of the most anticipated games of a loaded Week 10 slate of the 2026 college football season, quarterback Devon Dampier accounted for four total touchdowns, two rushing and two passing, to lift No. 4 Utah to a 28-20 victory over No. 8 BYU on Saturday, Nov. 7 at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City, Utah. The win was sealed with two seconds remaining, when Nate Ritchie intercepted a Bear Bachmeier desperation heave in the end zone. It was Bachmeier's fourth interception of the day, matching the BYU quarterback's total from his team's first eight games this season. More: Utah has a message for CFP, SEC and Big Ten: Deal with us now The turnovers proved to be costly on a day in which the Cougars outgained the Utes by a 391-328 margin and averaged 6.1 yards per play. The win kept Utah's unbeaten record intact, improving the Utes to 9-0 overall and 6-0 in the Big 12 heading into a big game next week at No. 22 Arizona. The victory snapped Utah's three-game Holy War losing streak and was their first win in the rivalry since 2019. BYU, meanwhile, fell to 7-2 overall and 4-2 in the Big 12, narrowing its path to the Big 12 championship game and a spot in the College Football Playoff. Get real-time updates, scoring plays, turning points and expert analysis throughout as BYU takes on Utah. Follow along as USA TODAY Sports provides live updates, highlights, injury news, key plays and instant breakdown from the Cougars-Utes showdown. Utah-BYU analysis As painful as it would have been, Utah could have afforded to withstand a loss to BYU, thanks to an 8-0 start to the season that gave coach Morgan Scalley's team enough cushion to make a Big 12 championship game or College Football Playoff appearance even without an unbeaten record. But after three losses in a row to the Cougars in a series in which they hadn't won since 2019, the Utes really needed this one. And even beyond the bragging rights they earned with a 28-20 victory, they got a win that will resonate. With just three games remaining in the regular season, Utah is 9-0, with only one game left against a team that's in the top 25 of the US LBM Coaches Poll. Thanks to the win over the Cougars — which was made possible at least in some part by Bear Bachmeier's four interceptions — the Utes have a two-game lead for the second and final spot in the Big 12 championship game. To make things sweeter, by beating BYU, they significantly narrowed the Cougars' playoff chances, though a road to the 12-team field is certainly there. A big win in front of a home crowd to boost your own championship dreams while putting your hated foes' on life support? It's what rivalries are all about. Just about everything is on the line. That includes serious College Football Playoff consideration. Utah is undefeated and has a straight line to the Big 12 championship. BYU has a big win over Notre Dame, but also a loss to unranked UCF that complicates its resume. What happens here will affect the top of the playoff committee's rankings this week. Here are five matchups in the game we're keeping a close eye on. 1. BYU's Biggest Danger BYU's biggest vulnerability remains its struggling rushing attack. The Cougars managed just 47 rushing yards against Arizona State, averaging 1.6 yards per carry. Injuries along the offensive line and uncertainty surrounding running back LJ Martin's availability only add to the concern. Utah ranks 22nd nationally in rushing defense, allowing just 101.4 yards per game. If the Utes shut down BYU's ground game, quarterback Bear Bachmeier could face constant pressure in obvious passing situations. If so, that could make BYU's offense predictable and allow Utah's defense to dictate the game. 2. Here is how I'm wagering college football Week 10. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . No. 9 BYU @ No. 3 Utah This Holy War might be the holiest of them all: Utah hosting bitter rival BYU, with the winner in the driver's seat for a Playoff spot. It’s the first time both teams have been ranked in the top 10 for this matchup, and I can’t wait to start the day with this one. I think BYU might win outright. It has been tested with its win over Notre Dame just a few weeks ago. Yes, it lost to UCF the following week in a typical trap game — big home win followed by a road conference game. Otherwise, the Cougars have handled business, even though the scores don’t seem that impressive. BYU is built on defense. It is 13th in yards per play and it limits explosives. It does not rush the passer all that well, but against Utah’s rushing attack, that might not be needed. BYU’s defense already faced a high-powered offense in the Irish and limited it to a negative EPA rushing day. Utah’s offensive production slowly ticked down when conference play started, but it did bounce back last week against a poor Cincinnati defense. Utah has played one defense in the same realm as BYU and that was Houston. Utah struggled to score, only putting up 21 points with seven of those happening super late after forcing a Houston turnover. Will the BYU offense find a groove against Utah? (Getty Images) It’s fair to also believe BYU’s offense might struggle in this game. However, it appears the Cougars are getting stud running back LJ Martin back, and they are much better when Martin is on the field. He’s averaging almost eight yards a carry with 20% of his rushes going for 10+ yards. Utah’s defense is the typical physical front against the run, but BYU is the best offense the Utes have faced all season. Utah’s pass rush concerns me. It is 80th in pressure rate and unless it blitzes, it isn't able to get to the quarterback. Seems less than ideal against BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. I see these teams as even. They are both defensively based with an offense that wants to run the ball. That’s too many points in a game like this. I’ll take BYU to cover. Schwartz's Pick: BYU -4.5 No. 5 Alabama @ No. 14 LSU In the newly-released CFP rankings, Alabama is fifth and is an underdog at LSU by almost a touchdown. I do lean towards LSU at -6, but that number feels big. Instead, I’m going to fade Alabama’s offense in this game. Alabama is facing its fourth straight difficult defense, and in the first three games, we’ve seen the offensive efficiency drop. Quarterback Keelon Russell is nearing the end of his first season as a starting quarterback, and he’s been mostly excellent for his age. However, he has struggled the last three weeks outside the end of the Texas A&M game. Against Georgia, Tennessee and A&M, he completed only 60% of passes with just four passing touchdowns and three interceptions. Alabama’s beat-up offensive line has allowed 11 sacks in the three previous games. Now, the Tide play an LSU defense that’s first in sacks per pressure and 11th in pressure rate. The Bama offensive line and Russell were noticeably affected by the environment in Tennessee, and now they are at LSU. I feel most comfortable with Alabama not scoring much in this game. away.headline: BYU RB LJ Martin manages just 24 yards in loss to Utah
away.blurb: Having suffered an ankle injury against TCU on Oct. 3, Martin missed the Cougars' last four games. In his absence, BYU 's rushing attack was poor, proving too much to overcome in a loss to unranked UCF on the road. With a return date goal of Nov. 7 versus the Utes, Martin realized the goal and suited up in Salt Lake City. By game's end , Martin had carried the ball seven times for just 19 yards, though he did reach the end zone on a nifty fake reverse trick play from four yards out. He also caught one pass for five yards, for a grand total of eight touches for 24 yards and a touchdown. In the lead-up to the BYU Cougars ' Holy War matchup with the Utah Utes in Week 10, there was chatter throughout on running back LJ Martin 's injury status. But if him suiting up was supposed to swing the odds in BYU's favor, it shouldn't have. A majority of that production came in the first half, as Martin's impact was largely muted in the second half as backup Sione Moa took a bulk of the carries along with quarterback Bear Bachmeier. We may never know why that was, as Martin hardly saw the field in the final 30 minutes. It's likely that his ankle was giving him troubles, potentially re-aggravating it at some point. Regardless of the 24 total yards and a touchdown, Martin at full strength is good enough to be the best offensive player in the conference. In 2025, he was named the Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year after rushing for 1,300 yards and 12 touchdowns. That version of Martin was not on the field on Saturday against Utah, and it played a massive part in the Cougars being defeated. away.blurb: On Wednesday night, the BYU football program provided the first official injury update for LJ Martin ahead of a top 10 matchup with Utah. Martin is "doubtful" for the game against the Utes. The "doubtful" designation is reserved for the players that have a 25% chance to play. However, just a few minutes before the injury report came out, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Martin is considered "questionable" for this weekend. The "questionable" designation is reserved for players with a 50% chance to play. Thamel reported that if Martin returns, "he's not expected to be 100% and could be limited." Thamel added more information, saying "[Martin is] trending to dress, be available, and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later this week." Martin was back practicing on Tuesday, according to Aaron Roderick. The last time he played was in early October against TCU. If Martin can't go, BYU will turn to Preston Rex who was not available for the ASU game. Rex had a breakout game against Notre Dame before suffering an injury against UCF. If Saleapaga isn't available, expect more sets with three wide receivers. That would leave Walker Lyons on the field for most of the game. If Evan Johnson can't play, BYU will turn to Jayven Williams and Therrian Alexander III at cornerback. Williams and Alexander shut down two of the best wide receivers in the Big 12 last week. They are more than capable of holding it down on the outside. The bigger question will be who BYU plays at nickel. The Cougars started Cannon DeVries at that spot to start the season, but DeVries has primarily been used for punt return duties since he suffered an injury. The ASU game was the first time DeVries had seen defensive snaps since suffering the injury. He played 14 snaps. LJ Martin and Evan Johnson Officially Ruled Out for BYU Against ASU If Martin returns, it would be the first time BYU has had its full compliment of running backs since the season opener. Most of the time, BYU had three safeties on the field. BYU averaged 2.7 safeties on the field at a time against ASU. True freshman Kennan Pula has seen his role grow over the last few weeks. He played 24 snaps against the Sun Devils. home.headline: BYU RB LJ Martin manages just 24 yards in loss to Utah
home.blurb: Having suffered an ankle injury against TCU on Oct. 3, Martin missed the Cougars' last four games. In his absence, BYU 's rushing attack was poor, proving too much to overcome in a loss to unranked UCF on the road. With a return date goal of Nov. 7 versus the Utes, Martin realized the goal and suited up in Salt Lake City. By game's end , Martin had carried the ball seven times for just 19 yards, though he did reach the end zone on a nifty fake reverse trick play from four yards out. He also caught one pass for five yards, for a grand total of eight touches for 24 yards and a touchdown. In the lead-up to the BYU Cougars ' Holy War matchup with the Utah Utes in Week 10, there was chatter throughout on running back LJ Martin 's injury status. But if him suiting up was supposed to swing the odds in BYU's favor, it shouldn't have. A majority of that production came in the first half, as Martin's impact was largely muted in the second half as backup Sione Moa took a bulk of the carries along with quarterback Bear Bachmeier. We may never know why that was, as Martin hardly saw the field in the final 30 minutes. It's likely that his ankle was giving him troubles, potentially re-aggravating it at some point. Regardless of the 24 total yards and a touchdown, Martin at full strength is good enough to be the best offensive player in the conference. In 2025, he was named the Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year after rushing for 1,300 yards and 12 touchdowns. That version of Martin was not on the field on Saturday against Utah, and it played a massive part in the Cougars being defeated. home.blurb: On Wednesday night, the BYU football program provided the first official injury update for LJ Martin ahead of a top 10 matchup with Utah. Martin is "doubtful" for the game against the Utes. The "doubtful" designation is reserved for the players that have a 25% chance to play. However, just a few minutes before the injury report came out, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Martin is considered "questionable" for this weekend. The "questionable" designation is reserved for players with a 50% chance to play. Thamel reported that if Martin returns, "he's not expected to be 100% and could be limited." Thamel added more information, saying "[Martin is] trending to dress, be available, and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later this week." Martin was back practicing on Tuesday, according to Aaron Roderick. The last time he played was in early October against TCU. If Martin can't go, BYU will turn to Preston Rex who was not available for the ASU game. Rex had a breakout game against Notre Dame before suffering an injury against UCF. If Saleapaga isn't available, expect more sets with three wide receivers. That would leave Walker Lyons on the field for most of the game. If Evan Johnson can't play, BYU will turn to Jayven Williams and Therrian Alexander III at cornerback. Williams and Alexander shut down two of the best wide receivers in the Big 12 last week. They are more than capable of holding it down on the outside. The bigger question will be who BYU plays at nickel. The Cougars started Cannon DeVries at that spot to start the season, but DeVries has primarily been used for punt return duties since he suffered an injury. The ASU game was the first time DeVries had seen defensive snaps since suffering the injury. He played 14 snaps. LJ Martin and Evan Johnson Officially Ruled Out for BYU Against ASU If Martin returns, it would be the first time BYU has had its full compliment of running backs since the season opener. Other Injury Updates on BYU Starters BYU also provided injury updates on key starters Roger Saleapaga and Evan Johnson. Saleapaga left the game against ASU with an injury, and Johnson suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury against UCF. Johnson did not play against Arizona State last weekend. Most of the time, BYU had three safeties on the field. BYU averaged 2.7 safeties on the field at a time against ASU. True freshman Kennan Pula has seen his role grow over the last few weeks. He played 24 snaps against the Sun Devils. Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State , but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations. Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning ? Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean. Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia , Kentucky and Oklahoma . Texas vs. Missouri prediction, picks The best unit on this field is the Texas defense. Regardless of the health status of star edge rusher Collin Simmons, the Longhorns should be able to slow down a Missouri offense that hasn't faced a swarming unit of this caliber. If Arch Manning can just take care of the football like he did last week, Texas can lean on its defense, win the field position battle and put stress on a Missouri defense that showed real vulnerability in losses to Mississippi State and Ole Miss. The Tigers have been great at home the last few years, but they are a rung below Texas in overall talent level. While fans may already be looking ahead to next week's highly anticipated Death Valley matchup, the Tigers are certainly not a team to overlook . They're coming off a 34-10 blowout win over Arkansas — albeit, it was against the Razorbacks — and steamrolled the same Florida team that stunned Texas with a second-half comeback just a few weeks ago. Saturday's matchup carries significant postseason implications , both for the College Football Playoff and the SEC championship race, as both teams enter with identical 3-2 conference records. Here’s how the Texas Longhorns On SI Staff sees this one playing out. Matt Galatzan Texas has gotten back on track over the last two weeks, but various shortcoming are still very prevelent. Texas has struggled along offensive line, and as a result, the running game has suffered. Those issues have also caused a cascading effect on the passing game, making for an inconsistent product. To make things worse, things on the injury front don't look good for the Horns. Kade Phillips, Ryan Wingo and Graceson Littleton are all banged up but should play, while Colin Simmons and Cam Coleman are less likely to play, and Hollywood Smothers and Nick Townsend were both lost for the year. Texas can overcome these issues if the defense continues to perform at a high level. Ole Miss showed the blueprint to shut down the Tigers ' offense. If Texas can stay on schedule on offense and avoid a third-quarter collapse, I think they can get it done. Mississippi State sacked the redshirt junior six times last Saturday, and Texas now plays without left tackle Trevor Goosby, who suffered a season-ending knee injury against Ole Miss. “They average getting sacked nearly one out of every 10 dropbacks,” McElroy said of Texas. “That’s 126th because the breakdowns come from all over the protection.” The ESPN analyst said Texas has struggled when its receivers have to beat man coverage snap after snap, and he called Missouri’s cornerbacks “about as good as you find when it comes to playing that coverage week in and week out.” How does Texas reach 24 points? Wingo, a St. Louis native Missouri recruited out of high school, leads Texas with 36 catches for 470 yards, while Coleman, an Auburn transfer, leads the team with seven touchdown catches. McElroy’s route to 24 points runs through Wingo “in the catch-and-run game” against a Missouri defense he said sits “at or near the bottom as far as missed tackles,” plus “one Coleman shot over the top.” “But without it, Texas might be living on field goals, which is a dangerous recipe on the road,” McElroy said. A loss would send Texas to LSU next week with three defeats, a scenario ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum said could cause the Longhorns to “ collapse .” Texas visits Missouri at noon ET Saturday on ESPN. That meeting was the 2017 Texas Bowl. What should scare Longhorns fans is the 2026 version is tinkering on the edge of a disappointing bowl like that. Especially if they can't beat a team like Missouri. The Tigers are a good team. It's easy to see Missouri winning on Saturday. They're ranked just 11 spots below Texas in the College Football Playoff rankings and have the same record. And Mizzou has home field advantage. Then why is Texas a -3.5-point favorite. Because a fully functioning Texas team is better than Missouri. But this Texas team isn't fully functioning. First, the injuries are starting to pile up. It was announced this week that the Longhorns have lost running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend for the rest of the season. All-American right tackle Trevor Goosby is also out for the year. And UT has been without All-American EDGE Colin Simmons for weeks. In addition to trying to plug the injury holes, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian must also continue to work on the offense. At times it looks great. But its not trustworthy. Will Muschamp's defense will need to stand tall for a third game in a row if the offense can't get it going. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas walks into this Missouri game needing the win to feel confident about their CFP chance heading into LSU. Missouri is a relative unknown, with losses to both Mississippi schools but a dominating win over Florida. Jamal Roberts and the run game leads the way, averaging just over 160 rushing yards/game. Austin Simmons has become a riser in this upcoming NFL Draft, flashing his elite arm talent every week. Texas was able to get a win over Tennessee earlier this season, but I don't see this as a task that's comparable. Missouri is capable of performing at a high level on both sides of the ball, especially the front seven defensively. It's difficult to imagine this Texas offense to trade punches with Missouri, especially on the road, so I'll take the Tigers to possibly end Texas' CFP hopes. Final Score: Texas 20, Missouri 23 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns will take on Missouri this Saturday in their latest SEC clash. The Tigers are off to an impressive 6-2 start and, like Texas, are 3-2 in conference play. Texas will need Arch Manning to be at his best and for the defense to shine. Last week, the Longhorns defense held Mississippi State to three points and 187 total yards. If the Longhorns can replicate that performance, another win could be on the horizon. This should be a game that Texas can win as they look to improve their playoff odds. Final Score: Texas 31, Missouri 13 Trey Luerssen's Prediction When this year's schedule came out, I thought the game against Mizzou might be the toughest to forecast. But it's even tougher now, because we're not sure which team will actually show up on either side of the ball. Both teams have had some big wins and some real clunkers. How much will Texas miss Smothers and Townsend? Can the defense slow down the Tigers offense? Which version of quarterback Arch Manning will show up in Columbia? For four games in a row, Texas has jumped out to an early lead and then coughed it up by the end of the third quarter. UT is 2-2 in that stretch. A coin flip. Twice the dam broke and twice it didn't. I think the defense will save the offense again. The tricky road trip begins Saturday against No. 19 Missouri and extends to Nov. 14 against No. 15 LSU. But Texas, listed at No. 7 in this week's CFP rankings , can't afford to look past a rugged Missouri squad that likes to run the ball and lean on its defense. The beat-up Longhorns have lost All-American left tackle Trevor Goosby for the season and must overcome a rash of other injuries entering Saturday's game. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Missouri Tigers. GOLDEN: Defense is Texas' pathway to playoff, but Arch Manning's legs are useful, too | Golden No. 10 Texas (6-2, 3-2 SEC) at No. 19 Missouri (6-2, 3-2) When: 11 a.m. Saturday Where: Faurot Field in Columbia, Miss. TV/radio: ESPN, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: Pack a jacket, because temperatures could be in the low 40s at kickoff and won't climb out of the 50s. Former coach Gary Pinkel turned Missouri into a Big 12 contender in the 2000s, but the Tigers could never get over the hump against a Texas squad in the heart of its golden era under Mack Brown . They came closest in 2008, when Missouri quarterback Chase Daniel and Texas quarterback Colt McCoy combined for 655 yards passing. McCoy accounted for four total touchdowns for a Texas team that went 12-1 but missed out on a chance to play for a national championship after a wrenching last-second loss at Texas Tech in Week 9. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Know the foe: Missouri Last week: Beat Arkansas, 34-10 Players to watch: QB Austin Simmons , a 6-foot-4, 220-pound senior, once seemed like the heir apparent at Ole Miss but transferred to Missouri this past offseason after the emergence of current Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss. He's averaging 244 yards passing a game on 63.3% passing with 17 passing touchdowns compared to just two interceptions. RB Jamal Roberts , a 6-foot, 215-pound senior, stepped into a starring role after All-SEC running back Ahmad Hardy got shot in the leg at a concert in May and missed the first seven games of this season following surgery. Roberts leads the SEC with 1,005 yards rushing and averages 5.3 yards per carry. LB Nicholas Rodriguez, a 6-foot, 225-pound junior, leads the SEC with 11 tackles and game and forced a fumble in last week's win over Arkansas. His sideline-to-sideline range anchors the Tiger run defense. Central Texas connections: None. When Texas has the ball The Longhorns have issues running the ball, and Missouri prides itself on stopping the run. The ground game doesn't seem like a recipe for Longhorn success, especially since Texas running backs Hollywood Smothers and Derrek Cooper remain limited by injuries. Longhorn RB Raleek Brown followed up a 157-yard game against Ole Miss with just 30 yards rushing in last week's win over Mississippi State, and Missouri ranks third in SEC play by allowing only 104.8 yards rushing a game. When Missouri has the ball The Tigers like to pound the ball, especially since Hardy made his season debut last week against Arkansas. If Hardy can find the form that helped him rush for 3,000 yards and 29 TDs over his first two collegiate seasons, he'll team with Roberts in arguably the best backfield in college football. But Texas gives up yards on the ground grudgingly; the defense allows just 98.4 yards per game rushing in SEC play, which ranks only behind Georgia. The secondary may be the most beat-up unit on the squad, which is saying something for the bruised and battered Longhorns. Graceson Littleton , an elite slot corner, will likely miss the game. So could starting cornerback Kade Phillips. That was a devastating result after Trevor Goosby — a pillar of the Longhorns' offensive line who is projected to be a top-10 pick in next year's draft — had already been ruled out for the remainder of the year. The injuries for Texas could be the straw that breaks the camel's back, with the Longhorns already struggling on offense, limping into Week 10 ranked 74th in Success Rate, 95th in Explosiveness and 129th in Havoc Allowed. Arch Manning's inconsistencies have made it difficult for Texas to stay ahead of the sticks, leaving the offense vulnerable to stalling out early on in drives. While Coleman and Wingo are expected to play at less than 100%, Smothers' outlook looks bleak, forcing the Longhorns to lean more heavily on Raleek Brown . When given the opportunity, Brown has been a consistent source of production in the Texas backfield, averaging nearly five yards per carry. With question marks lingering over the offense, the Longhorns will need to continue to play at a high level on the other side of the ball in order to keep their hopes of making the playoffs alive. Luckily for Texas, the defense has been the strength of the team this season, entering Week 10 ranked in the top 25 in Success Rate, Explosiveness, Finishing Drives and Havoc. Missouri 's hot start to the year is arguably one of the bigger surprises of the season, with the Tigers just one win away from clearing the over on their regular-season win total while sitting 1.5 games back from first in the SEC conference standings. Austin Simmons ' resurgence under center has played a major role in Missouri's success, throwing just two interceptions in eight games while averaging 8.1 yards per throw. While Simmons has been able to thrive through the air, the Tigers' running back room has yet to find its footing, ranking near the bottom of the board in Rush Success Rate and PPA. When Jamal Roberts is unable to hit the ground running, opposing defenses can stretch out their linebackers across the middle, smothering Simmons' passing lanes at multiple levels of the field. While the Tigers do give up explosive plays at an alarming rate, they are able to successfully keep their opponents out of the end zone, giving up just 3.03 Points per Opportunity. While Simmons has been able to play far better than initially expected, negative regression is looming large over the Tigers' quarterback as he battles it out against a secondary that excels in coverage, per its top-30 mark in Dropback EPA Allowed per play. With the Longhorns keeping a body on Missouri's pass-catchers' hips, the amount of Havoc in Simmons' throws will increase, leading to an uptick in his total number of Turnover-Worthy Plays. Even with Hardy back on the field, it's tough to envision the star running back being able to quickly shake off the rust, making the Tigers far too one-dimensional. Barring a sudden turnaround on the ground, Texas will be able to drop more bodies back in coverage, making it easier to create disruptions. Colin Simmons has also been upgraded to questionable, yet it remains to be seen if the Longhorns' edge rusher will suit up on Saturday. While the Longhorns do generate pressure at a high rate, Simmons would help pull defensive attention to the edge, freeing up more space in the interior to help the middle of the defensive line collapse the pocket. With no clear path for success, expect Missouri to be held to early outs at a consistent rate, chipping away at the Tigers' total number of scoring opportunities. away.headline: Texas' Hollywood Smothers Reportedly Out for Rest of CFB Season with Knee Injury
away.blurb: Smothers wasn't available for games against Tennessee and Ole Miss, and he has been an ineffective option as part of a rotation with running back Raleek Brown. Smothers carried the ball just four times for minus-6 yards before entering the medical tent against Mississippi State last week. Texas running back Hollywood Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a torn MCL, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported. Smothers was among the top running backs in the 2026 transfer class after rushing for 939 yards with seven touchdowns at NC State last season. He was expected to be an explosive addition to the Longhorns offense and began the season as the starting running back, but he has been hampered by injuries throughout the season. The Longhorns entered the season with high expectations, but inconsistent performances from quarterback Arch Manning and a bevy of injuries have threatened to derail their campaign. Texas was ranked No. 1 after starting the season with a 4-0 record, but they now sit as the No. 7 ranked team after two consecutive losses against unranked Oklahoma and Florida. Texas will need Brown to carry a larger workload as they fight to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive moving forward, but the injuries are continuing to mount. The Longhorns have already lost star left tackle Trevor Goosby to a season-ending injury, and the team's injury report for their upcoming game against Missouri is nearly as long as a drug store receipt. Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian will need players to step up in order for the team to live up to their preseason expectations. The margin for error is slim, and those injuries could prove to be critical during their upcoming road games against two ranked opponents, No. 18 Missouri and No. 14 LSU. As it has since SEC play started, Mizzou ruled out running back Malae Fonoti, who is out for the season, right tackle Josh Atkins, who Eli Drinkwitz said he does not expect to be available this year, and tight end Gavin Hoffman. Despite what I expect to be a hostile environment at Minnesota's Huntington Bank Stadium, the Bruins enter Saturday's Big Ten clash as 5.5-point road favorites, with a moneyline of -192. UCLA vs Minnesota Odds, Betting Line, Point Spread UCLA vs Minnesota Spread : UCLA -3.5, Minnesota +3.5 UCLA vs Minnesota Over/Under : 38.5 Total Points UCLA vs Minnesota Moneyline : UCLA ML -182, Minnesota ML +152 UCLA has been the biggest surprise of the college football season, as first-year head coach Bob Chesney has ripped through a relatively difficult conference schedule and is now one of just three undefeated teams at 8-0. This has all happened despite losing quarterback Nico Iamaleava to a season-ending injury against Oregon , I think the loss of the former Vol made this Bruins bunch even better, thanks to the spectacular play of backup Ty Dieffenbach . While many initially saw Iamaleava's injury as a major roadblock to their playoff quest, the signal-caller had been extremely turnover-prone and objectively overrated nationally. Nico had thrown just four passing touchdowns all year before getting hurt and turned the ball over six times during that stretch. In his absence, Dieffenbach has thrown for 683 passing yards while turning the ball over only once — a vital attribute for a squad that relies heavily on its defense. Running back Wayne Knight has also been spectacular for Chesney's rushing attack, racking up 680 yards on the ground at an impressive 6.2 yards per carry. Knight's 12 rushing touchdowns rank seventh nationally, and I expect him to play a major role in what should be a difficult road atmosphere. Knight is one of several key players Chesney brought to UCLA from James Madison, and he leads a versatile backfield that also features Anthony Woods and Jaivian Thomas. The Bruins are battle-tested and continue to impress each week, and this matchup against Minnesota will undoubtedly be a difficult challenge if UCLA is to advance to 9-0. This Big Ten showdown will have major playoff implications for the Bruins as the regular season comes to a close. The season has been up and down for the Golden Gophers , who enter their Week 10 matchup with a 5-3 record. Minnesota has looked inconsistent in head coach PJ Fleck's 10th season at the helm, losing two of its last three contests after an impressive 4-1 start. Junior quarterback Drake Lindsey has looked impressive in his second season under center, throwing for 1,592 yards through the air over the first eight games. Running back TJ Thomas leads the rushing attack with 379 yards and is the feature tailback in a backfield that also features Darius Taylor and Xavier Ford . The Gophers have been far more efficient through the air, though, with a receiving corps that includes senior wideout Noah Jennings and speedster slot option Javon Tracy, who have combined for 855 receiving yards. This will be a huge test for defensive coordinator Danny Collins' unit, which has looked very impressive over the first nine weeks, with opponents scoring just 20.5 PPG on average, ranking 35th in the FBS. Collins' aggressive, heavy-blitzing 4-3 base schematics will be tested against an extremely well-balanced UCLA offense that rarely turns the ball over. While this clash is undoubtedly more significant for UCLA, it still matters for a Gopher bunch looking to finish on a strong note before bowl season. While UCLA has looked spectacular in its first year under Chesney, I expect Saturday to be very difficult for the Bruins, who will be under pressure in front of a rowdy Gopher fanbase. UCLA boasts one of the premier defenses in college football, ranking seventh in opponent yards per game, 13th in opponent passing yards per game and 10th in opponent rushing yards per game. Fleck's defense is also extremely dominant, ranking inside the top 25 in several defensive metrics. In a game where I expect UCLA to start sluggish on the road, with an earlier start time than the Bruins are accustomed to, I favor backing under 7.5 points in the first quarter at -135 in what I expect to be a low-scoring defensive battle. There's no real mystery to what UCLA does. It blasts away, with the ground game, gets just enough from the passing game to get by, and then it relies on the defense to take care of everything else. It starts with third down stops. Only Nebraska – at least before the loss to Illinois – is better at defensively on third downs than the Bruins. That allows UCLA to dominate the time of possession battle, the rested defense forces a ton of takeaways, the offense capitalizes … repeat. However … Why Minnesota Will Win UCLA runs well, Minnesota doesn't. Minnesota can throw well, UCLA doesn't. Other than that, these two do almost all of the same things. You want third down defense? Minnesota is sixth in the nation, allowing teams to convert just 28% of their chances. Time of possession? The Gophers aren't as good as UCLA, but they're fine, usually keeping the ball for close to 32 minutes per game. And then there are the takeaways – Minnesota is good at that, too. The temperature should hover around 40 degrees and feel more like 32ish for the entire game in Huntington Bank. UCLA will be pushed and tested, and Minnesota will take advantage of that early, but the score will be kept low throughout, and the Bruins will still be alive in the second half, when the ground game starts to take over. Our Alabama vs. LSU prediction and college football picks back Lane Kiffin and the Tigers to snap their Saban Bowl losing streak as Alabama seeks its fourth straight series victory on the first Saturday in November. The Crimson Tide visit Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., where LSU enters as a 5. 5-point favorite in Death Valley. Kickoff is scheduled for 3: 30 p. m. ET on ABC on Saturday, Nov. 7. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs LSU: LSU -5.5 The last time LSU won the Saban Bowl, Nick Saban was Alabama's head coach and Lane Kiffin was still beloved at Ole Miss . That will change Saturday when Kiffin's surging Tigers take advantage of a Crimson Tide team that's looked like a far cry from its No. 5 College Football Playoff ranking. With LSU's defensive ferocity and Alabama's offensive struggles, I like the Tigers to cover up to -6.5 at home against the Tide. Not only has LSU's defense been wrecking opponents, but the Tigers' offense has been on fire too, with Sam Leavitt fourth nationally in QBR (85.3) and 12th in adjusted completion percentage (79.5%). Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris (480 receiving yards and seven TDs in his last four SEC games) are a problem for an Alabama defense that's ranked 78th in pass success rate (44.3%). Alabama vs LSU Over/Under pick: Under 52.5 This game isn't one of the must-watch games in my college football Top 25 predictions this week because I'm expecting offensive fireworks; it's because of the talent on these defenses. LSU's defense is especially loaded, and with Alabama's struggles against quality defenses, I would play the Under at 51.5 or better. The Tigers are second nationally in sacks (34) , and Keelon Russell hasn't managed pressure well. He's been sacked the ninth-most in the country (22) and has a 20.4% pressure-to-sack rate. But I don't expect an offensive onslaught from LSU either. This is the best defense the Tigers have faced this season, with Alabama ranking 20th nationally in available yards percentage (37.7%) and 14th in net adjusted EPA per play. Alabama vs LSU prop: Alabama TT Under 23.5 Alabama's offense has no identity, and Kalen DeBoer and Ryan Grubb don't seem to know how to fix it. Against LSU, I like the Under on the Crimson Tide's team total at 21.5 or better . Alabama continues to deal with two key injuries on the offensive side of the ball, with both center Racin Delgatty and wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams questionable for this game. If those two don't play, Alabama will struggle to score even 20 points. The Crimson Tide don't have consistent playmakers outside of Coleman-Williams, and LSU's defense brings the heat, ranking fourth nationally in havoc rate (22.2%) . Alabama vs LSU combo Alabama has gotten off to slow starts and failed to cover in three straight games as a result. In the Crimson Tide's last three games, it trailed Georgia 10-0, trailed Tennessee 9-0, and trailed Texas A&M 14-10. If Alabama gets off to another slow start and trails LSU, the Tigers' defense will pin their ears back and go to work. LSU ranks eighth nationally in pass success rate on defense (36%) and has one of the most lethal pass rush duos in the country, Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross (58 combined pressures and 13.5 sacks). Death Valley is one of the hardest places to play, and with Alabama's broken offense, I don't expect the Tide to score much early against this opportunistic LSU defense. Both Alabama and LSU come into the game with a record of 6-2, giving each team a chance to make a real statement . Each team is coming off a bye week, giving them more rest and time to prepare for this huge game. With SEC schedule changes coming, this matchup will be the last one played between the two teams on a yearly basis. This could add more emphasis for both sides to want to come away with the win. With this rivalry game kicking off in a few days, the Crimson Tide aren't being favored to come away with the win on the road. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Alabama only has a 43 percent chance of taking down LSU this week. Since the game is being played on the road, LSU is likely being favored, especially since Tiger Stadium can be so tough to play in. One of the bigger keys to the game for the Crimson Tide will be how quarterback Keelon Russell can perform. Alabama has all the confidence in the world in Russell, but he has been a little shaky at times this season. For the year, the signal-caller has thrown for 2,057 yards with 15 touchdowns and five interceptions through the air. On the ground, Russell has made his presence known for this team, rushing for Russell has proven to be very impactful for Alabama, even with his limited experience as a starting quarterback. If Russell can handle the hostile atmosphere that LSU will throw at him, the Crimson Tide could have a strong chance to win the game. Alabama is going to need Russell to play more like he did against Kentucky earlier in the season, rather than how he looked against Tennessee a few weeks ago. The signal-caller have a lot of talent, but he can sometimes make poor decisions with the football. LSU has a very strong defense, and this will be a major challenge for Russell to overcome this week. But if Alabama is going to reach the heights that this program wants to get to this season, Russell is going to have to be able to handle these types of games.
