The loser of this game may miss out on the college football playoff and given the Tigers' remaining strength of schedule, this is a must-win for LSU. Both teams are coming off a bye week, so we should expect a chess match between Lane Kiffin and Kalen DeBoer . Some would say this is a must-win for Alabama despite being the #5 ranked team in the new playoff rankings. The Tide's two best wins came against Kentucky when the Wildcats were unranked and a routing of #16 Mississippi State which sent Kamario Taylor and the program into a spiral. A win at LSU would solidify Alabama's spot, but a loss puts their season in the hands of others. Alabama plays Vanderbilt, Chattanooga, and Auburn following LSU; one of the easiest strength of schedules in P4. Alabama trailed 20-17 to Texas A&M before rattling off 14 points in the fourth quarter to avoid three-straight losses. Keelon Russell threw for 311 yards and three touchdowns, and the defense forced three turnovers in the win. Alabama has won three straight against LSU and won 12 of the last 15. Sam Leavitt and Kiffin will try to break the streak in his debut season. LSU is coming off two back-to-back big wins before the bye week. The Tigers crushed Mississippi State 31-0 and Auburn 38-17. Sam Leavitt threw seven touchdowns and ran for another in that two-game span, plus Jackson Harris caught four of those touchdowns and totaled 263 receiving yards. LSU's defense has only allowed 281 yards through the air in those two games as well, so nothing should come easy in Death Valley for one of the best home defenses in the country. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Alabama vs LSU Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Time: 3:30 PM Eastern Site: Tiger Stadium City: Baton Rouge, LA TV/Streaming: ESPN | ABC Game Odds for Alabama vs LSU The latest odds as of Wednesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: LSU Tigers (-225), Alabama Crimson Tide (+185) Spread: LSU -5.5 (-110) Total: 52.5 points #5 Alabama Crimson Tide Head Coach: Kalen DeBoer 2026 Record: 6-2 (4-2) Offensive Points Per Game: 38.2 (12th) Defensive Points Per Game: 21.2 (T-44th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 27th 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 14th The Alabama Crimson Tide Offense: Keelon Russell and Alabama found their groove in the fourth quarter against Texas A&M, and I was particularly impressed with Rico Scott. Alabama's offense has been without Ryan Coleman-Williams , so Scott has been one of the players asked to step up. Scott caught a career-high six passes for 156 yards and a season-long 48-yard reception. Russell threw for 311 yards, but the rushing attack struggled with 2.4 yards per carry on 28 carries for 68 yards. Alabama Player to Watch on Offense: QB Keelon Russell Keelon Russell had a bounce-back performance against Texas A&M. Russell threw two touchdowns in the fourth quarter to pull the Tide up, then seal the deal. He finished with 311 passing yards, three touchdowns, and one interception on 19-of-30. Alabama has been without Ryan Coleman-Williams for the last two games (TENN, TX A&M), but he could return this week, which would significantly boost Russell's output. The Alabama Crimson Tide Defense: Alabama's defense forced three turnovers last week: two interceptions and one fumble (forced three). The Tide held the Aggies to 278 total yards and 2.9 yards per rush, which is light-years better than the 150 rushing yards and 3.7 yards per carry allowed to Tennessee. In the last three games, Alabama allowed 20, 26, and 20 points, but were outgained in yards in their two losses to Tennessee and Georgia. Alabama Player to Watch on Defense: LB Caleb Woodson In the last three games, Caleb Woodson has racked up the tackles. He had nine versus Georgia, 11 at Tennessee, and 10 against Texas A&M for 30 of his team-leading 63 tackles. Woodson has four games with double-digit tackles this season after having one in three seasons with Virginia Tech. Woodson's career-high is 72 tackles, which he will likely pass this weekend, and another sack (2) or interception (1), and he will have career highs in both categories. Expect to hear Woodson's name early and often. The Tigers have found a balance between Dilin Jones and Sam Leavitt . Jones has 39 total carries in the last two games for 175 yards, and he's also caught 12 passes for 85 yards, for 51 total touches compared to 83 dropbacks for Leavitt. Jackson Harris has also caught four touchdowns and put up 263 yards in the last two games, so the stars have been shining for LSU. LSU Player to Watch on Offense: QB Sam Leavitt Sam Leavitt might be playing his best football of the season. In the last two games, Leavitt has thrown seven passing touchdowns with no picks and a rushing touchdown. In his first six games of the season, he had at least one pick in all of them, so this is a pleasant surprise for LSU. Leavitt has 25 total touchdowns on the year (17 pass, 8 rush) and will be a handful in this game with his dual-threat ability. Alabama has only allowed two quarterbacks to throw for two-plus touchdowns on their defense this season, and Leavitt has accomplished that in five straight games. If LSU wants to win, Leavitt will have to be on his A-game, and he went into the bye week on fire. The LSU Tigers Defense: At home, LSU's defense has allowed 10, 14, 6, 14, and 0 points for 8.8 points per game! That's one of the best marks in the country, and lately, the Tigers have played their best ball with 17 points allowed over the last two games and 140.5 passing yards per game. LSU has only forced one turnover in that dominant two-game stretch, and the Tigers will likely need to win the turnover battle to beat Alabama. LSU's defense ranks fifth in pressure and first in coverage grades per PFF, and with the Tide ranking 54th in pass blocking, LSU could find success getting to Keelon Russell . LSU Player to Watch on Defense: DE Princewill Umanmielen Princewill Umanmielen got back in this sack column against Auburn! While it was only a half-sack, it still counts toward his team-leading 8.5 sacks that ranks third in the country. Umanmielen's 12 TFLs rank tied eighth in the nation, and he ranks second in the SEC in both TFLs and sacks. He trails only Texas' Collin Simmons (16 TFLs, 10 sacks). picks.headline: ‘If they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs LSU
picks.blurb: ‘If they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs LSU - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Zach Ragan · AtoZ Sports Tue, November 3, 2026 at 8:43 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The LSU Tigers will host the Alabama Crimson Tide in a huge SEC showdown in Baton Rouge this weekend. LSU will host Alabama this upcoming Saturday in what's a de facto College Football Playoff elimination game. Alabama and LSU both have two losses. It's possible that the loser of this game could still get into the playoff with three losses — it depends on how the rest of the season plays out — but the winner will be the only one that controls its own destiny moving forward. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, made his score prediction for the game, and he has LSU leaving Tiger Stadium with a 27-20 win. McElroy thinks LSU's defensive line will be able to win the battle up front. "I'm taking LSU to win the game 27-20," said McElroy. "I do think the under is in play, but it's really going to come down to Alabama's offensive line. If Keelon Russell gets time, they can win this game in Baton Rouge. But if they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb for the Crimson Tide." McElroy noted that most of the sacks Alabama has given up this season have come from Russell holding the ball too long. Alabama and LSU will kick off at 2:30 PM CT/3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) Getty Cole Sullivan · HEAVY Fri, November 6, 2026 at 3:22 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The No. 5 Alabama Crimson Tide will travel to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, on Saturday afternoon for a massive SEC showdown against the No. 14 LSU Tigers. Ahead of the matchup, both teams have released their injury reports. While the Tigers will be without star linebacker Whit Weeks, Alabama also has several key players whose status remains in doubt. One player in particular who could be monitored up to kickoff is star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams. He suffered an injury several weeks ago in the loss to Georgia and has remained sidelined since. Lane Kiffin Makes Prediction for Coleman-Williams Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer has been relatively quiet about providing in-depth injury updates. However, according to LSU head coach Lane Kiffin, he believes he knows whether the Alabama star will play or not. During his weekly radio show Thursday night, Kiffin predicted that Coleman-Williams would play against the Tigers. "I would expect him to play," Kiffin said, adding that Alabama has a track record of getting athletes back on the field super fast. DeBoer's Latest Update on Coleman-Williams Coleman-Williams has carried a questionable tag throughout the week. While DeBoer likely knows whether his star wide receiver will play or at least has a good idea of his status, there's a good chance Alabama waits until Saturday to make a final decision. "A lot of these guys from Zabien Brown to Ryan Coleman-Williams, EJ [Crowell], Racin [Delgatty], Terrance Green in particular — those guys are all working on the football field," DeBoer said earlier this week, via ESPN's Alex Scarborough. "They're not all in the exact same spot, but they're all out there going through workouts. Some are taking team reps, some are taking non contact reps." Mandatory Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brooke Benedict · LSU Tigers On SI Sat, November 7, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As LSU takes on SEC rival Alabama on Saturday for a high-stakes matchup, fans are anticipating a talent show that will crown the winner with a major advantage in the postseason. With both teams 6-2 this season, the final stretch of the season, starting this Saturday, will show who's the best playoff contender . The staff of LSU Tigers on SI has made their picks for the LSU vs. Alabama game. LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin walks on the sideline during the first quarter against the Kentucky Wildcats at Kroger Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect College Football Playoff hopes will be on the line Saturday. LSU and Alabama would love to notch a signature win. Alabama's opportunistic secondary could trouble Sam Leavitt and the offense. If Leavitt protects the ball and the defensive line takes advantage of a potentially vulnerable Crimson Tide offensive line, LSU should win. Tiger Stadium will be deafening, and I think the Tigers will make a statement on Saturday. LSU 35, Alabama 24 I think that the Tigers win a close one at home. This freshly healthy Alabama squad will be a tough challenge for these LSU Tigers, but I think that the LSU defense will come up with a pick-six late in the game to seal their victory. LSU 31, Alabama 28 LSU and Lane Kiffin are ready to take down Alabama. For Kiffin, he's 0-5. For LSU, a three-year losing streak will end. Sam Leavitt has made the jump and taken care of the football and looked sharp through the air, with LSU having solid o-line play to lead the way in establishing the run and attacking Alabama's defense in every way. The Tigers' defense is ready for the challenge too. With Alabama missing some key pieces on the o-line, and LSU's dominant pass rush, the matchup easily favors the Tigers. LSU 45, Alabama 21 Brooke Benedict LSU and Alabama have shown a similar weakness this season, as both teams reveal critical system errors and momentum failures when trailing in a game. Alabama showed this against Tennessee and LSU has shown this against Ole Miss, both major opponents this season. As Saturday's matchup brings the same level of competition, it's key that both teams don't let the score turn lopsided. With the home-field advantage, I think LSU will be able to gain the momentum early, and Alabama will lose key momentum in the environment of Tiger Stadium. LSU 28, Alabama 20 While LSU vs. Alabama isn't a "storied" rivalry, it's perhaps some of the best football that gets played each year, and this matchup will be no different. Kiffin is looking for his first signature win with LSU, and if Sam Leavitt continues to play the same way he has the last two weeks, I expect it to happen. LSU 38, Alabama 30 Hannah Garcia I think that LSU is going to pull out the victory this weekend just because, for one thing, Alabama is missing their top receiver, Ryan Coleman Williams. Despite the fact that they have a really good quarterback in Keon Russell, I do think that the vital piece of their offense being missing will affect their game this weekend. I also think that our defense is a lot stronger than theirs is; we are holding opponents to fewer points per game than their team is, despite both defenses being really good. In terms of our offense, I think that Sam Levitt has been on the up and up the past couple of games; he hasn't thrown any interceptions, and he's looking more like the 2024 CFP quarterback that he once was. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon in a pivotal game in the Big Ten and CFP race Getty Images Week 10 of the college football season has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Oregon live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Ohio Stadium -- Columbus, Ohio TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State vs. Oregon prediction, picks The Ducks have to pick up where they left off offensively to have a chance here, and they should push the tempo a bit and try to stretch things out in the air. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. But the 34-26 win doesn’t change the fact that a 6-2 Buckeyes squad vs. a 5-3 Ducks team presents a much different matchup than their No. 1 and No. 2 preseason rankings suggested. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Tennessee game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Kentucky vs. Tennessee game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction chrisbeasmore · SB Nation Tue, November 3, 2026 at 2:23 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky Football moved up one spot to No. 8 in the AP Top 25 Poll despite not playing a game this past weekend. One major reason for the Wildcats' rise was Ohio State's loss to USC on Saturday. Kentucky is now 7-1 overall and 5-1 in SEC play, making the Wildcats one of the most surprising teams in college football this season, especially under first-year head coach Will Stein. The last time Kentucky took the field, the Wildcats defeated Vanderbilt 34-17 at home. However, they got off to a slow start, falling behind 10-0 before turning things around and taking the lead into halftime. Kentucky eventually took care of business to secure another SEC victory. Now, the Wildcats will hit the road to Knoxville this weekend to face the Tennessee Volunteers. Kentucky's most recent road game came against Oklahoma, where the Wildcats escaped Norman with a 21-13 victory. Kentucky will look to replicate that performance against Tennessee, but the Volunteers' defense has been one of the nation's best and will present a significant challenge. Tennessee Volunteers (6-2, 3-2) Tennessee has an impressive defense, but the Volunteers also have a talented running back in DeSean Bishop. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow him down, as he can make opposing defenses pay if he gets into a rhythm. Meanwhile, Tennessee's quarterback situation has been a concern, with the Volunteers relying on George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon. The two quarterbacks have different styles. MacIntyre tends to be more conservative, often targeting receivers near or behind the line of scrimmage, while Brandon is more willing to push the ball downfield. It will be interesting to see which quarterback Tennessee turns to on Saturday against Kentucky. At wide receiver, Mike Matthews has emerged as the Volunteers' primary target, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards. Defensively, Tennessee has been impressive, recording 35 sacks, eight interceptions, and nine fumble recoveries this season. Kentucky will need to protect the football and avoid costly mistakes to have a chance to leave Knoxville with a victory. The Wildcats will likely need a near-perfect performance on both sides of the ball. Turnovers could quickly swing the momentum in Tennessee's favor, especially with the Volunteers playing in front of their home crowd at Neyland Stadium. Tennessee had an impressive 26-10 victory over Alabama at home. However, the Volunteers have also suffered a couple of notable losses, including a 20-17 defeat to Texas at home and most recently a heartbreaking 27-24 loss to South Carolina on a game-winning field goal. With both teams coming off a bye week, Kentucky will have an opportunity to prepare for Tennessee's defensive strengths. Still, winning on the road against a talented Volunteers team will be a difficult task. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Tennessee Volunteers Location: Neyland Stadium — Knoxville, Tennessee Date: Saturday, November 7 Time: 6:15 p.m. ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 33.2% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction Kentucky enters this matchup at 7-1 overall and 5-1 in SEC play, having won six consecutive games since its home loss to Alabama in the second game of the season. The Wildcats will look to keep that momentum going, improve to 8-1 overall and 6-1 in conference play, and strengthen their case for a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, the challenge does not get any easier this weekend. Kentucky must travel to Knoxville to face a Tennessee team with a dominant defense and plenty of motivation of its own. The Volunteers are also coming off a bye week and will be ready to respond after their loss to South Carolina. While Kentucky has been playing some of its best football of the season, I believe the Wildcats' winning streak comes to an end in a close, low-scoring contest. Tennessee's defense will make things difficult for Kentucky's offense, and the home-field advantage at Neyland Stadium could ultimately prove to be the difference. Final score: Tennessee 27, Kentucky 21. How do you see this one playing out?

Despite entering Saturday's Week 10 clash with a 7-1 overall record on the season, Kentucky remains a 6.5-point road underdog with a +188 price tag to pull off the outright upset. Kentucky vs Tennessee Odds, Spread, Line Kentucky vs Tennessee point spread : Kentucky +6.5 (-110), Tennessee -6.5 (-110) Kentucky vs Tennessee over/under : 50.5 (-110o / -110u) Kentucky vs Tennessee moneyline : Kentucky +188, Tennessee -225 In one of the bigger surprises of this college football season, the Wildcats have emerged as one of the best teams in the entire country in head coach Will Stein's first year at the helm. Kentucky senior QB Kenny Minchey has been phenomenal in his first season in Lexington after spending three years at Notre Dame and throwing the ball only 30 times there. Minchey has thrown for 1755 yards and 14 touchdowns over the Wildcats' first eight games this season with just one turnover. Freshman WR Kenny Darby has been Minchey's favorite target with over 500 yards and three touchdowns. Stein's rushing attack has been effective too, with senior tailback CJ Baxter rushing for nearly 500 yards and eight touchdowns. The Wildcat offense is averaging just shy of 33 points per game this season, but will get its most difficult test on Saturday against an elite Tennessee pass rush. Kentucky's defense has thrived under defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, who has built an aggressive, havoc -creating unit that has fared well against some elite SEC offenses this season. The Wildcats lead the SEC in interceptions and pass breakups, boasting an elite secondary led by veteran safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell. While its front seven struggled early this season, Kentucky has improved drastically in the trenches over the course of the season. The 8th-ranked Wildcats are in a great spot to potentially qualify for the playoffs, but still must face several difficult conference opponents, starting with the Vols in Week 10. The 16th-ranked Volunteers put their postseason hopes on the line as Josh Heupel's bunch looks to evade a third loss this season that would very likely ruin their playoff resume. After a very promising 6-1 start to the season despite an ongoing QB battle between George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon , Tennessee was defeated on the road at South Carolina this past weekend for the Vols' second loss of the year. Now they face a must-win game, with lingering questions about whether Heupel will stick with MacIntyre under center or return to top-ranked freshman QB Brandon. Regardless, betting markets have made their stance quite clear, with Tennessee currently listed as a near-touchdown favorite despite the Wildcats' breakout 7-1 campaign. While WR Mike Matthews has recorded over 500 receiving yards this season, Tennessee has relied far more on its rushing attack, with tailback DeSean Bishop rushing for 957 yards and 11 touchdowns, ranking sixth and ninth in all of college football, respectively. However, the Vols' defense has thrived all year, particularly at home, where it allows SEC opponents the third-fewest PPG in the conference (16.25). Jim Knowles was brought in as defensive coordinator this past offseason after serving in the same capacity for Penn State , and has significantly improved a unit that fell to 81st in the country in EPA (Expected Points Added) last season. Tennessee's defense boasts an elite linebacker corps ranked in the top 10 nationally, featuring Edwin Spillman, Amare Campbell, Arion Carter, and Jeremiah Telander. While the Vols' defense has carried this team for most of the season, especially at home in Knoxville, their offense will need to show up in this matchup, given how impressive Michey has been at avoiding turnovers. I expect this to be one of the best matchups in an absolutely loaded Week 10 slate. While I have been very impressed with the Wildcats offense and a much-improved defensive unit, I expect the atmosphere to be quite chaotic given how difficult it is for SEC foes to escape Neyland Stadium in Knoxville with an outright victory. The Vols boast an extremely dominant pass rush that should give Kentucky's offensive line fits considering how much that unit has struggled to contain elite edge pressure. That said, I feel betting markets are giving Tennessee a tad too much credit given their fragile situation at QB. In what I expect to be a pretty closely contested matchup, I'm going with the Volunteers moneyline. I got it at -210 earlier this week as soon as the line opened, and while I typically don't lay that much juice on a moneyline, especially considering the volatility of betting college football, I have confidence Tennessee gets the outright win, but laying close to a touchdown versus a red-hot Wildcat bunch is far from ideal. Though Tennessee's moneyline has since crept up to -230, I still don't mind playing the Vols at that number. Pick: Tennessee ML (-225, FanDuel )

On any other Saturday, and in any other time slot, this would be the biggest game of the day, with huge SEC and CFP implications. This starts an hour before it's on, but by the second quarter, Georgia-Ole Miss and Miami-Notre Dame will both be ramping up while the Cats and Vols are humming. This will still earn a front-and-center spot, though. As good as Tennessee has been – including a relatively dominant 26-10 win over Alabama – it's coming off a 27-24 loss to South Carolina, and it's one loss away from being in a really, really tough spot to stay alive for the CFP. Kentucky got destroyed by Alabama in Week 2, but it's on a six-game winning streak. It pulled off great 35-34 wins over both LSU and South Carolina, and it won at Oklahoma. It has breathing room with just one loss, but with a rough finishing kick, beating Tennessee would be gigantic. Kentucky vs Tennessee: Quick Hits Tennessee has just one home game left after this, hosting LSU between road games at Texas A&M and Vanderbilt. Kentucky gets two of its last three games at home, hosting Florida next week and with Louisville to close, going to Missouri in between those two. Tennessee has won the last five meetings, going back to a 34-7 UK win in 2020. But this Wildcat team just doesn't give anyone anything to work with. Kentucky is No. 1 in the SEC in fewest penalties and No. 1 in turnover margin. The Wildcats have only been hit with 15 penalties over the last five weeks, and they haven't turned it over in any of the last four games. On the flip side, Tennessee gets flagged an average of 7.6 times per game, and while turnovers aren't a big problem, it gave the ball away eight times over the last four games. Why Tennessee Will Win Tennessee has to keep the mistakes to a minimum, and it has to keep the offense moving. It doesn't have to take any big chances against a Kentucky defense that's good against the run but doesn't do much to come up with third down stops. The Volunteer pass rush is the best in the nation, and it should be disruptive in the Kentucky backfield, but it really is about the offense. Tennessee's ground game has been fantastic – it's 16th in the nation – and that's a jumping-off point. Kentucky vs Tennessee Prediction, Betting Lines The Vols are 6-0 when the offense generates more than 320 total yards, and 0-2 when it doesn't. Only Vanderbilt and Youngstown State failed to get at least 340 yards against the Kentucky defense. Yes, Kentucky is for real. It's well coached, sharp as a tack, and it's one of those teams that just knows how to win. But with two weeks off after the South Carolina loss, the rejuvenated Vols will make a massive statement in both the SEC and College Football Playoff chases with a strong performance. But history tells us that Tennessee is always the wrong direction for Kentucky football, which has lost 38 of the previous 41 games in the series. picks.headline: Rece Davis Predicts Notre Dame Playoff Problem Ahead of Top-5 Miami Showdown
picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Notre Dame Playoff Problem Ahead of Top-5 Miami Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Notre Dame could find itself in the same College Football Playoff predicament that ended its 2025 season if it can’t beat No. 1 Miami on Saturday, according to ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis. Davis made the case on ESPN’s College GameDay Podcast with co-hosts Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel, saying the No. 4 Fighting Irish (7-1) would be in “ very much the same situation as a year ago ” with a loss. Rece Davis on Notre Dame’s resume Notre Dame Fighting Irish head coach Marcus Freeman reacts during the first half against the Brigham Young Cougars | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis said that split will shape the debate over the Irish. He expects them to stay in the field unless the Hurricanes blow them out, but he doesn’t see the questions about their resume going away. “I think Notre Dame will still be OK absent getting run out of the stadium, which I cannot conceive of happening,” Davis said. “So it’s going to be a little bit different than last year, but the argument, the discussion, is going to be the same if they don’t win this game.” He added: “When you get down to who did you play and who did you beat, especially the who did you beat portion of who did you play, they won’t have much on the paper.” Why does Notre Dame’s schedule matter? General view as Brigham Young Cougars fans celebrate on the field after the game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. The Irish beat Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State, Purdue, North Carolina, Stanford and Navy. After Miami, they close with Boston College, SMU and Syracuse, who are a combined 14-10 and unranked. Notre Dame does carry a protection it lacked last year. The College Football Playoff guarantees the Irish a spot if they finish in the top 12 of the final rankings. A loss to Miami would test that cushion, though, because Notre Dame would sit at 7-2 with no win over a ranked opponent and no ranked teams left on its schedule. Miami vs. Notre Dame stakes Miami Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal celebrates after defeating the Florida State Seminoles | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last season, Miami and Notre Dame both finished 10-2, and the selection committee used the Hurricanes’ 27-24 win in Week 1 to award them the final at-large spot. The Irish were the first team out and declined a bowl invitation. Last season, Miami and Notre Dame both finished 10-2, and the selection committee used the Hurricanes’ 27-24 win in Week 1 to award them the final at-large spot. The Irish were the first team out and declined a bowl invitation. Notre Dame athletic director Pete Bevacqua said at the time, “ We feel like the playoff was stolen from our student-athletes.” Davis called the rematch “another little delicious subplot” and said Notre Dame’s frustration “wasn’t necessarily just directed at Miami.” Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman made “ leave no doubt ” the program’s mantra for 2026 after the snub. Saturday gives the Irish that chance against an 8-0 Miami team that leads FBS at 47.6 points per game, while Notre Dame’s defense leads FBS at 236.1 yards allowed per game. The committee releases its first College Football Playoff rankings of the season Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Miami vs. Notre Dame kicks off Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Notre Dame has one of the better offensive lines in college football but has its work cut out against this Miami defensive front. The Hurricanes are allowing just 2.4 yards per rush attempt this year, which means Notre Dame likely won't be able to play the same ball possession type game it likes to. That means CJ Carr's moment is now: Miami has a pass defense that has surrendered huge numbers in narrow escapes against both Florida State and North Carolina. South Bend will be the epicenter of the college football universe on Saturday night when the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes roll into town to face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish. We won't get to see Malachi Toney in action, but our Miami vs. Notre Dame prop picks for this heavyweight bout focus on the showdown between elite quarterbacks Darian Mensah and CJ Carr. For more college football picks and analysis, check out Rob Paul's Miami vs. Notre Dame predictions ahead of kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. Best Miami vs Notre Dame props Prop pick #1: CJ Carr Over 4.5 rush attempts I gave out this same prop when Notre Dame faced BYU, and CJ Carr came through. I'm backing it again, up to 55%, for many of the same reasons. It starts with the game plan. This Miami defense ranks second in EPA per rush but 110th in EPA per pass. That means we'll likely see fewer handoffs and more dropback opportunities. That also puts Carr up against a Hurricanes front that ranks 15th in pass-rush grade, per PFF, and 29th nationally in sack rate. Carr has shown this season that he's not afraid to scramble. Factor in sacks counting as rush attempts, and he should clear this total for the fifth time in seven contests. Prop pick #2: Micah Gilbert Over 31.5 receiving yards Jordan Faison leads all Notre Dame receivers with 56 targets, while Jaden Greathouse and Micah Gilbert are tied with 33 targets apiece. But Gilbert is the player being undervalued here, and I'm backing him up to 54%. Miami's secondary isn't just struggling in coverage; it's also struggling to make tackles in the open field. Gilbert has the best yards after catch per reception (5.5) of Carr's top three targets and ranks second behind Faison in yards per route run. Gilbert is also the most reliable of the three, securing 72.7% of his targets. He's averaging 70.4 receiving yards in the six games in which he's run at least 20 routes. He's a bargain with a receiving yards line that's less than half of Faison's 69.5-yard total. Prop pick #3: Darian Mensah Over 1.5 passing touchdowns With Malachi Toney sidelined, Darian Mensah has an opportunity to take another step toward the Heisman tonight, and I'm backing him up to 55% to throw multiple touchdown passes. Not only do the Hurricanes rank third in red-zone scoring, but only Notre Dame has a higher offensive Eckel rate than Miami this season. As well as Notre Dame defends, the Irish are depleted on the back end heading into this game. Defensive captain Drayk Bowen is out at linebacker, and the secondary will be without DJ McKinney and Tae Johnson. The Irish gave up three touchdown passes to UNC's Billy Edwards, one of the few quality passers they've faced this season. Mensah leads the nation in passing efficiency and completion rate, and getting him at this number is a gift. home.blurb: Which made it all the more gut-wrenching when the Heisman Trophy front-runner came down with an injury during practice the week leading up to the Hurricanes ' mammoth matchup against Notre Dame . Reports said Toney suffered a high ankle sprain on Wednesday, Nov. 4, and that he would undergo surgery, putting not only the showdown with the No. 6 Fighting Irish out of the question, but the rest of his stellar season in jeopardy. According to the Cleveland Clinic , high ankle sprains occur when the ligaments that attach the tibia to the fibula near the foot are torn or damaged. Recovery takes six to eight weeks, though the Clinic says it might take longer for athletes to return to play. In order to maintain control of its College Football Playoff destiny, Ole Miss will have to knock off Georgia for the third time in the program’s last four matchups. With a loss, the Rebels will put their season resume in the hands of the playoff committee with little optimism of returning to meaningful postseason play. Defense will be the difference in the matchup this year, with Georgia having one of the best in the country ( ranked No. 2 by SP+ ), and Ole Miss' being one of the worst in the SEC. Georgia vs Ole Miss Over/Under pick: Under 56.5 Though both games between these teams last year were full of points, Georgia's defense should keep it relatively low-scoring this time around, and I would play the Under at 55.5 or better . With no Lacy for Ole Miss, it'll put even more on Chambliss, who has frequently had to carry the team this season, and we saw that approach fall flat against Texas. However, Georgia's offense hasn't been lighting up the scoreboard lately either, averaging just 23.6 points per game in its last three outings. So while this is one of the must-watch matchups in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , it's not because I'm expecting another shootout. The Rebels beat LSU and Missouri , but were blown out by Florida and fell behind so quickly against Texas that they couldn't dig themselves out. With 4.5 40-yard dash speed and nearly 34-inch arms, Cole has earned his nickname of "Tarantula." Look for the Bulldogs to spy Chambliss with him and use him as a blitzer too; he leads Georgia in pressures (24) and pass-rush win rate (17.4%). With Cole hunting Chambliss and the Bulldogs' defense ranking top 20 in rush success rate (37.8%), Ole Miss will struggle to find the end zone. away.blurb: Arguably Georgia's biggest game of the season is against Ole Miss, and that matchup has finally arrived. The Bulldogs are looking for some revenge after the Rebels knocked them out of the playoff last season, but on top of that they are hoping to strengthen their hold on the SEC with a win this weekend. Georgia has gotten a lot of great injury news heading into their matchup with Ole Miss. Wide receiver Isiah Canion has been out since the second game of the season, but on Thursday he was removed from their injury report and appears to be making his return this weekend. Running back Chauncey Bowens could also be making his return this weekend as well. He was injured a few weeks ago and when it initially happened some people in the program feared it could've been season ending, He hasn't been fully cleared to play against Ole Miss yet, but on Friday he was listed as probable to play on their official injury report. Ole Miss on the other hand isn't getting as lucky on their injury report. Star running back Kewan Lacy will miss his second game in a row this weekend after being hurt at Texas. EDGE Kam Franklin and linebacker Keaton Thomas are game-time decisions for Ole Miss, but if either player is ruled out that would be difficult for the Rebels to overcome. Ole Miss on the other hand is only 4-4 against the spread this year. The Rebels are much better against the spread at home against top 15 teams though. So while the odds are in Georgia's favor heading into this game, history shows that Ole Miss stands a great chance at winning this game. home.blurb: Arguably Georgia's biggest game of the season is against Ole Miss, and that matchup has finally arrived. The Bulldogs are looking for some revenge after the Rebels knocked them out of the playoff last season, but on top of that they are hoping to strengthen their hold on the SEC with a win this weekend. Georgia has gotten a lot of great injury news heading into their matchup with Ole Miss. Wide receiver Isiah Canion has been out since the second game of the season, but on Thursday he was removed from their injury report and appears to be making his return this weekend. Running back Chauncey Bowens could also be making his return this weekend as well. He was injured a few weeks ago and when it initially happened some people in the program feared it could've been season ending, He hasn't been fully cleared to play against Ole Miss yet, but on Friday he was listed as probable to play on their official injury report. Ole Miss on the other hand isn't getting as lucky on their injury report. Star running back Kewan Lacy will miss his second game in a row this weekend after being hurt at Texas. EDGE Kam Franklin and linebacker Keaton Thomas are game-time decisions for Ole Miss, but if either player is ruled out that would be difficult for the Rebels to overcome. So much is on the line for both teams this weekend, so here is all the information fans need to know to watch. What time do Ole Miss and Georgia play? Kickoff between Ole Miss and Georgia is scheduled for 7:30 pm EST on Saturday, Nov. 7. This game is being played in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, MS. How to watch Ole Miss and Georgia Georgia and Ole Miss will air on ABC. This game can also be streamed on Fubo TV and the ESPN app as well. The spread for nearly every college football game will shift at some point throughout the week from where it originally opened. That however didn't happen with this matchup. Georgia originally opened as a three point favorite over Ole Miss, and as of now they are favored by 3.5 points over the Rebels. Georgia is 6-2 against the spread so far this season. Ole Miss on the other hand is only 4-4 against the spread this year. The Rebels are much better against the spread at home against top 15 teams though. Over the past four years they are a perfect 6-0 at home against the spread and straight up against top 15 teams which includes their 28-10 win over Georgia in 2024. So while the odds are in Georgia's favor heading into this game, history shows that Ole Miss stands a great chance at winning this game. Georgia vs Ole Miss injury updates Georgia and Ole Miss have turned into quite the rivalry over the last few years. They are nowhere near becoming a traditional rivalry, but the last few years they have met multiple times with so much on the line each time they've played. home.blurb: Friday Ole Miss vs. Georgia Injury Report: Keaton Thomas Probable - The Rebel Walk FRIDAY Ole Miss vs. Georgia Injury Report: Keaton Thomas Probable, Franklin Questionable Recent ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss linebacker Keaton Thomas is probable for Saturday night's game against No. 2 Georgia after being questionable on Thursday, according to the SEC's Friday availability report. Defensive end Kam Franklin remains questionable. The report was posted at 7:10 p.m. CT on Friday. Ole Miss' list of players who are out did not change, with running back Kewan Lacy and eight others ruled out again. Georgia, meanwhile, moved three players from questionable to out: inside linebacker AJ Kruah , safety Tyriq Green and defensive lineman Joseph Jonah-Ajonye . Keaton Thomas moves up to probable Thomas, a linebacker, was questionable on both Wednesday and Thursday and is now probable for Saturday night. That is the only change to the Ole Miss availability designations from Thursday. Cornerback Jalyn Crawford and safety MJ Preston remain probable, and no other Rebels are listed. Kam Franklin remains questionable Franklin has carried the questionable tag all week and has not been cleared with kickoff about 23 hours away. He has 25 tackles, including 15 solo stops and 10 assists, along with 5.0 tackles for loss, two sacks, a pass breakup and a fumble recovery he returned for a touchdown through eight games this season. He was named a leader of the defense in our September feature on Franklin . Without him, Ole Miss would lose one of its best pass rushers and run stoppers against a Georgia offense that scores 41 points per game. Georgia's report got shorter on the questionable side and longer on the out side. Kruah, Green and Jonah-Ajonye were all questionable on Thursday and are now out, joining outside linebacker Amaris Williams, who has been out all week. Tight end Elyiss Williams remains questionable. Wide receiver Thomas Blackshear and running back Chauncey Bowens were questionable Thursday and are now probable. Kickoff is set for 7:45 p.m. ET on the SEC Network. Florida is favored by -6.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -215. Oklahoma, meanwhile, enters as a +6.5 underdog and is +176 on the mineyline to pull off the upset. The over/under sits at 44.5 total points. Here's my Oklahoma vs. Florida prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 7. Oklahoma vs. Florida Pick: Florida -6.5 My Florida vs. Oklahoma best bet is on the Gators to cover the spread as home favorites in The Swamp. Oklahoma vs Florida Odds Oklahoma vs Florida point spread : Florida -6.5 (-102), Oklahoma +6.5 (-120) Oklahoma vs Florida over/under : 44.5 (-118o / -104u) Oklahoma vs Florida moneyline : Oklahoma +176, Florida -215 Oklahoma head coach Brett Venables is off to a rough start to his fifth season in Norman, as his Sooners enter their Week 10 matchup against Florida with a 4-4 overall record on the season. Over the first eight games of the season, Oklahoma has alternated wins and losses. If the pattern is to hold true, the Sooners should leave Gainesville with an outright victory, which is certainly a tall order for a team that just got their doors blown off by South Carolina by 17 points at home. Despite how poorly the Sooners have been playing, Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer has still looked somewhat impressive under center in his second season under Venables. Mateer has aired it out for 1,835 passing yards this season while also throwing 13 touchdown passes, ranking inside the top 40 in the nation on both accounts. Following the Sooners' Week 9 loss to the Gamecocks, Oklahoma offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle was fired, which leaves a ton of uncertainty about the direction of an offense that lacks elite offensive playmakers. While the Sooners offense is scoring just 22 points per game this season, Oklahoma's defensive unit has been impressive, which isn't very surprising considering Venables' experience as a top-tier defensive coordinator. The Sooners defense is allowing opponents just 20.8 points per game on average, ranking 38th in college football in that metric. For a Florida offense that has struggled to find an identity at times this season with some concerns at the quarterback position, the Sooners' clear path to reigning supreme in Week 10 is to play to their strengths in a slow-paced, low-scoring affair. It has been a very up-and-down first season in Gainesville for Florida head coach Jon Sumrall. The Gators enter Saturday night's matchup with Oklahoma with a 5-3 overall record after losing three of their last four games following a very impressive 4-0 start to the season. Despite signature wins over Ole Miss and Texas, Florida has been very volatile over the last several weeks, making it quite difficult to anticipate which version of the Gators we'll see week to week. While the Gators' losses to Georgia and at Missouri are quite understandable, Florida got its doors blown off by a LaNorris Sellers-led Gamecock bunch in a result that single-handedly destroyed the team's College Football Playoff aspirations. It was a very hot start to the campaign for quarterback Aaron Philo , which took a turn for the worse over the last few weeks. Sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. started in a win over Texas when Philo was hurt and is expected to make the start for the Gators on Saturday night. For a Sumrall offense that has really struggled throwing the football, the Gators will undoubtedly need to rely heavily on star tailback Jadan Baugh , who's in the midst of a very impressive season thus far. Baugh leads Florida's rushing attack with 801 yards on the ground through the team's first eight games, which ranks 17th in all of college football. The junior back has also found the end zone a whopping 13 times this season but will get a tough schematic matchup against a well-coached Oklahoma stop unit. Venables made his career off his prowess as a defensive specialist, playing a major role in Clemson winning two National Championships. Given Florida's struggles at the QB position, I fully expect the Sooners to stack the box to try and contain Baugh at all costs. The Gators have been far worse on the defensive side of the ball, with their eight opponents this season scoring 28.1 PPG, ranking outside the top 100 in the country. For a Florida team that has played itself out of the College Football Playoff picture over the last several weeks, Sumrall's bunch will surely still be looking to make a statement in front of its home crowd on Saturday night. For two teams that have struggled all year to find consistency, this makes for a difficult handicap, especially with all the questions surrounding the Gators' quarterback situation heading into Week 10's matchup. While I'm having a tough time justifying laying nearly a touchdown on a squad that just benched its starting QB last weekend, I ultimately feel Sumrall's bunch has a definitive edge largely due to Florida being a far superior team when playing in front of a home crowd in Gainesville. I lean Florida to cover its -6.5 spread in Saturday night's matchup. Pick: Florida -6.5

picks.headline: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Luka's explosive night LeBron's new reality Knicks defend Taylor Swift NFL news, live updates Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:18 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When we last saw Oklahoma and Florida play, the Sooners rolled 55-20 in the 2020 Cotton Bowl over a high-powered Gator team that lost to eventual national champion Alabama in an epic SEC Championship. The other meeting was the BCS Championship at the end of the 2009 season, when Tim Tebow and the Gator defense took down Heisman-winner Sam Bradford and the amazing Sooner attack 24-14 for the national title. The stakes aren't as high this time around, but for a Florida program that's on the rise, and No. 24 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and for a 4-4 Oklahoma desperate to close strong, this will be intense. Oklahoma vs Florida: Quick Hits Oklahoma at 4-4, needs to win two of its last four to be bowl eligible. It hosts Ole Miss and Texas A&M after this before closing at Missouri. Florida is coming off the 27-8 loss to Georgia. It goes to Kentucky next, hosts Vanderbilt, and finishes at Florida State. Again, the first two meetings were in big bowl games. This is the first regular season matchup between the two. How To Watch Oklahoma vs Florida Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:45 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville, FL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Oklahoma Will Win The defense continues to fight the good fight. It had a problem in the 42-25 loss to South Carolina, but the defense is fantastic on third downs thanks to a pass rush that takes over games. But to beat Florida, you have to slow down the run. The Gators are 0-3 when running for fewer than 155 yards, and the Sooners give up just 107 yards per game. Only Mississippi State and, last week, South Carolina have been able to gash the Sooners for more. Why Florida Will Win Oklahoma's offense has a hard time running the ball. With a defense as good as the Sooners have, all the O has to do is keep it moving and not screw it up. But no running game means more pressing overall, and then come the mistakes. The Sooners only average 107 yards per game on the ground, and they just can't find any room to move. The Gators have to hold up, and then pounce on an Oklahoma attack that turned it over four times against both Georgia and Kentucky, three times against New Mexico, and twice against Michigan. Oklahoma vs Florida Prediction, Betting Lines It's stupid, but if you buy into these things, going back to the last two games of last season, Oklahoma is on a ten-game run of alternating wins and losses. The Sooners beat Texas, then lost to Kentucky, beat Mississippi State, lost to South Carolina, beat … Florida? The Sooners have the defense to hold up and make Florida struggle. The Gators got by Texas a few weeks ago, but it's been a struggle, losing three of the last four. Weird trends aside, this Oklahoma team really does have a way of rallying when it absolutely has to. The Sooners need to win two of their final four to earn bowl eligibility . With a new voice leading the offense, the Sooners are hoping for a turnaround to end the 2026 season. Jason Witten takes over an offense that has underachieved this season, given the number of returning starters along the offensive line and the weapons at returning quarterback John Mateer. How much better can Oklahoma be in a week is the question on everyone's minds. It's unlikely the Sooners will suddenly erupt on offense, but if they find more consistency, they'll have a chance to finish the season on a high note. So how will the Sooners perform in "The Swamp?" Our staff here at Sooners Wire picked this week's showdown between the Sooners and the Gators. There are just too many moving parts for Oklahoma to reliably believe the Sooners could win a road game in the swamp. The Sooners have made a change at offensive coordinator and the availability of a bunch of notable players on both sides of the ball are still in question. There's also the question of how Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer will play without Ben Arbuckle on the sideline for the first time in years. Even though Florida has a few issues to worry about as well, they're certainly not as dire as Oklahoma's at the moment. Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 James D. away.blurb: Off a disappointing loss to Georgia, the Florida Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) return home to face Oklahoma (4-4. 2-3 SEC) at The Swamp on Saturday, November 7 (7:45 p.m., SEC Network). The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. Can Florida football OL raise its level of play to protect Jones and get the run game back going? away.headline: Gators suspend starting DT Jeramiah McCloud for Oklahoma game
away.blurb: The status of McCloud, who is listed as out on the SEC's intitial availability report, will be re-evaluated after Saturday night's contest. A 6-foot-3, 294-pound sophomore from Georgia, McCloud has started five of eight games for the No. 24 Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) and has 22 tackles, second to senior Brendan Bett's 23, a team-high six quarterback hurries and three pass break-ups, tied for the team lead. Meanwhile, sophomore receiver Vernell Brown III is on track to miss his fifth straight game with a right knee injury after he was listed as doubtful. After Brown aggravated the injury during practice last Wednesday, his knee was drained Thursday. On Monday, medical staff performed a platelet-rich plasma procedure to try to accelerate healing. Receiver Bailey Stockton has filled the void , but he's listed as questionable after he led the Gators with eight receptions for 76 yards, including 41 after catch, and had 31 yards on two punt returns during last weekend's loss to Georgia. Also questionable is defensive end Emmanuel Oyebadejo, who has started four of the past five games and whose 4.5 sacks are tied for the team lead with Jayden Woods. The 6-foot-6, 303-pound Jacksonville State transfer also has five QB hurries and three pass break-ups. Three Gators other than McCloud are listed as out against Oklahoma, including starting right tackle Emekga Ugori. Senior Caden Jones, who started 10 games in 2025, will replace him. Tight end Evan Chieca also will not play against the Sooners. away.headline: Oklahoma Sooners starting offensive lineman trending toward return
away.blurb: Maikkula missed the South Carolina game with a lower-body injury suffered in the win over Mississippi State. As long as he maintains his probable status over the next couple of days, Maikkula will likely return to the starting lineup for the Sooners' road trip to face the Florida Gators . If he does, it'll be the most intact the Oklahoma offensive line has been this season after Heath Ozaeta returned to the starting lineup last weekend. The other big name to watch for the Sooners offense is tight end Rocky Beers. Beers is Oklahoma's second-leading receiver this season, with 34 receptions for 446 yards, and leads the team with four receiving touchdowns. Beers was listed as questionable for this Saturday. If he's not able to play, Hayden Hansen will get a vast majority of the tight end snaps, but the Sooners will need someone to step up in the pass-catching department. Also of note are the questionable tags on defensive backs Peyton and Eli Bowen. Peyton played last week against South Carolina, while Eli missed his fourth game in a row. Against a talented Florida wide receiver group, the Sooners defense would certainly benefit from their availability on Saturday. Florida will be without starting offensive tackle Emeka Ugorji this week. Two of their better wide receivers in Bailey Stockton (questionable) and Vernell Brown III are also in danger of missing the Week 10 contest. Stockton is second on the Gators in receiving, and Brown is third. Brown hasn't played since late September. Another name to keep an eye on is defensive end Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Oyebadejo is tied for the team lead with 4.5 sacks and is second in tackles for loss. He's also listed as questionable this week. "So he had a little thing done this morning to address hopefully some of the issue. The thing I want to make abundantly clear here is he's trying like hell to play. And the frustrating thing for him is he looked good Monday, Tuesday. He looked good most of Wednesday – had the little setback Wednesday at practice that at the time we felt like was a little setback, and then woke up Thursday with more swelling than we anticipated - and not as much range of motion. That's why on Wednesday when he left the building, he's like, 'I feel pretty good. I feel better than I thought I would.' After he had what was what we thought a little setback," Sumrall said Monday. "So listing think probable if I'm not mistaken last Wednesday, and then he got downgraded on Thursday to questionable if I'm not mistaken because Thursday is when he woke up and the swelling was more noticeable and the range of motion had decreased. So he was not available at practice today. I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because, like I said everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. Can Florida football OL raise its level of play to protect Jones and get the run game back going? home.headline: Florida has 7 players on initial SEC Availability Report for Week 10
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Four Gators are listed as out: defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson. McCloud is out due to a suspension, according to Swamp247 , while Robinson missed his first game of the season last week against Georgia. Listed as doubtful is wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed the last four games with a grade-1 PCL strain that he suffered against Ole Miss in Week 4 that was re-aggravated ahead of last week's Georgia game. "So he was not available at practice today," Jon Sumrall said on Monday . "I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The two players listed as questionable are wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Stockton has been dealing with a nagging foot injury but still played against the Bulldogs last week, finishing with 76 yards on eight catches. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas and offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis are listed as doubtful, while wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, defensive backs Peyton Bowen and Eli Bowen, tight end Rocky Beers and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu are listed as questionable, and offensive lineman Jake Maikkula is listed as probable. WR Bailey Stockton — questionable DL Emmanuel Oyebadejo — questionable OL Eddy Pierre-Louis — doubtful WR Jer'Michael Carter — questionable DL Kenny Ozowalu — questionable OL #69 Jake Maikkula — probable Questionable (50% chance to play) The initial SEC availability report for college football's Week 10 was released on Wednesday night; the Florida Gators have seven players listed, while the Oklahoma Sooners have a whopping 16. "Jeramiah McCloud has been suspended for this week's game against Oklahoma for conduct detrimental to the team. His status with the program will be re-evaluated after this week's contest," per a statement from a program spokesperson. Sumrall added what he called his "official VB3 statement": "He wants to play. He's doing everything he can to play. He's pissed off he can't play, and he's doing everything in his power to play. It's a real injury that we thought we were on the other side of that he had a setback last week, and it sucks. I mean, it freaking sucks for him." Oklahoma has eight players who are not expected to play on Saturday: linebacker Taylor Heim, defensive back Dakoda Fields, wide receiver Trell Harris, linebacker Cole Sullivan, tight end Trynae Washington, defensive back Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Ryan Fodje and Fred Hinton. home.headline: Gators suspend starting DT Jeramiah McCloud for Oklahoma game
home.blurb: The status of McCloud, who is listed as out on the SEC's intitial availability report, will be re-evaluated after Saturday night's contest. A 6-foot-3, 294-pound sophomore from Georgia, McCloud has started five of eight games for the No. 24 Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) and has 22 tackles, second to senior Brendan Bett's 23, a team-high six quarterback hurries and three pass break-ups, tied for the team lead. Meanwhile, sophomore receiver Vernell Brown III is on track to miss his fifth straight game with a right knee injury after he was listed as doubtful. After Brown aggravated the injury during practice last Wednesday, his knee was drained Thursday. On Monday, medical staff performed a platelet-rich plasma procedure to try to accelerate healing. Receiver Bailey Stockton has filled the void , but he's listed as questionable after he led the Gators with eight receptions for 76 yards, including 41 after catch, and had 31 yards on two punt returns during last weekend's loss to Georgia. Also questionable is defensive end Emmanuel Oyebadejo, who has started four of the past five games and whose 4.5 sacks are tied for the team lead with Jayden Woods. The 6-foot-6, 303-pound Jacksonville State transfer also has five QB hurries and three pass break-ups. Three Gators other than McCloud are listed as out against Oklahoma, including starting right tackle Emekga Ugori. Senior Caden Jones, who started 10 games in 2025, will replace him. Tight end Evan Chieca also will not play against the Sooners. home.headline: Florida vs. Oklahoma Thursday availability report
home.blurb: No. 25 Florida (5-3, 3-3 SEC) listed seven players on its second of four availability reports before facing Oklahoma (4-4, 2-3 SEC) in Gainesville on Saturday, and there were no changes from Wednesday's report. Florida ide receiver Vernell Brown III remains listed as doubtful, and defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud (suspended), tight end Evan Chieca , offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson ruled out for the contest. In addition, wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo are listed as questionable. Vernell Brown III – doubtful DL Jeramiah McCloud – out WR Bailey Stockton – questionable DL Emmanuel Oyebadejo – questionable As Swamp247 reported Wednesday night, McCloud is out for Saturday's contest due to a suspension, according to a program spokesperson, who provided a statement upon the revelation McCloud would miss the contest. "So he had a little thing done this morning to address hopefully some of the issue. The thing I want to make abundantly clear here is he's trying like hell to play. And the frustrating thing for him is he looked good Monday, Tuesday. He looked good most of Wednesday – had the little setback Wednesday at practice that at the time we felt like was a little setback, and then woke up Thursday with more swelling than we anticipated - and not as much range of motion. That's why on Wednesday when he left the building, he's like, 'I feel pretty good. I feel better than I thought I would.' After he had what was what we thought a little setback," Sumrall said Monday. "So listing think probable if I'm not mistaken last Wednesday, and then he got downgraded on Thursday to questionable if I'm not mistaken because Thursday is when he woke up and the swelling was more noticeable and the range of motion had decreased. So he was not available at practice today. I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because, like I said everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." Brown's situation has led to speculation outside the program that the legacy pass-catcher either opted out for the remainder of the season or isn't fully motivated to make his return to the field. Sumrall thoroughly dismissed the notion the sophomore was opting out of the remainder of the regular season amid UF's 1-3 record in October following the team's impressive 4-0 start. In a promising update revealed Wednesday, sophomore running back Duke Clark is set to return after missing Florida's last three games after suffering a foot injury against South Carolina .
